ITQAN:v2p381/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p381/r17.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p381/r17.claim: لدلوك الشمس means the sun’s decline from its zenith.
ITQAN:v2p381/r17.anchor:
﴿ غمة ﴾ شبهة
2499 ﴿ لدلوك الشمس ﴾ زوالها
2500 ﴿ شاكلته ﴾ ناحيته

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Migration, mentioned only briefly in al-Naḥl, is clearly commanded in this sūrah; the directions indicate that it is near.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It is evident from the way in which these directions are given that its time is near.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet is urged to persevere through prayer and supplication as migration nears, with glad tidings that truth will prevail.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It is indicated that the time of migration is near.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The command to establish prayer means to be diligent and vigilant in prayer.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: does not merely mean to offer the prayer. It means to show

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Duluk is the sun’s descent in three stages—midday, leaving the line of sight, and setting—marking zuhr, asr, and maghrib; lam marks time, conventionally meaning ‘at.’
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: There are three stages of this: one, when it descends from midday, second when it descends from the line of sight and third when it disappears from the horizon.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Ghasaq al-layl means the pronounced darkness at the start of night, the time of isha; Islahi takes the phrase as accusative by specification, emphasizing fajr rather than governing it with ‘establish.’
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: darkness of the first part of night when it becomes pronounced

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Qur’anic ‘recitation’ refers to Qur’an recitation at fajr, generally prolonged and audible; its being witnessed includes attentiveness of imam and followers and angels’ presence, mentioned in a hadith.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: also referring to a prolonged and audible recital of it in general terms.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Qur’an itself specifies the five prayer times and, in the next verse, tahajjud’s time; denying this after explicit mention merits a prayer for guidance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It is evident from this that the times of the five prayers is mentioned in the Qur’ ān itself.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Prayer times reflect the sun’s standing, kneeling, and prostration, as well as that of things receiving its light; Islahi cites 13:15 and 17:44 for cosmic prostration and glorification.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It is evident from the verse under discussion that the sun remains in the state of standing, kneeling and prostration in all the times of night and day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Creation’s posture calls people to pray and join its submission, yet humans bow to trivial things and act proud before their Lord, though those things themselves submit; the sun is a striking example despite being worshipped.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: All these creations of God invite human beings through their form and state that just as they kneel and prostrate before God, people too should do so

BURSEVI:v5p147/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p147/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p147/r1.claim: Duluk can mean the sun's decline, setting, paling, or slanting; the author takes the span as beginning at decline and reaching night darkness.
BURSEVI:v5p147/r1.anchor: {لدلوك الشمس} أي : وقت زوالها أو غروبها يقال : دلكت الشمس دلوكا

BURSEVI:v5p147/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p147/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p147/r2.claim: Each prayer is performed at its appointed time, not continuously across the interval; the span reaches the late-night prayer when twilight disappears.
BURSEVI:v5p147/r2.anchor: والمراد إقامة كل صلاة في وقتها المعين لا إقامتها فيما بين الوقتين

BURSEVI:v5p147/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p147/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p147/r3.claim: Qur'an of dawn means the dawn prayer; it is accusative either as an object of “establish” or as an exhortation, and is named for its recitation. The verse includes all five prayers.
BURSEVI:v5p147/r3.anchor: {وقرءان الفجر} أي : صلاة الفجر بالنصب عطفا على مفعول أقم

BURSEVI:v5p147/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p147/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p147/r4.claim: The dawn prayer is witnessed by night and day angels, recorded last by the night angels and first by those of day; dawn also displays God's power in the change from darkness and sleep to light and waking.
BURSEVI:v5p147/r4.anchor: يشهده ويحضره ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار ينزل هؤلاء ويصعد هؤلاء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r1.claim: After exposing the unbelievers' plotting, God turns the Prophet to worship and promises a station envied by all creation, teaching him not to occupy his heart with them; alternatively, the command follows the discussion of theology, resurrection, and prophethood as the noblest worship after faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r1.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى بعد أن ذكر كيد الكفار وسلى نبيه عليه الصلاة والسلام بما سلى أمره أن يقبل على شأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r2.claim: أقم الصلاة commands the prescribed prayers.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r3.speaker: عمر، ابن عمر، ابن عباس في رواية، أنس، أبو برزة، الحسن، الشعبي، عطاء، مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r3.claim: These authorities take the sun's dalūk as its decline from the meridian, the time of noon; Imami reports attribute this view to Abu Ja'far and Abu Abd Allah as well.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r3.anchor: وهو المروي عن عمر بن الخطاب وابنه وابن عباس في رواية وأنس وأبي برزه الأسلمي والحسن والشعبي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r4.speaker: أبو مسعود عقبة بن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r4.claim: A report says Gabriel came to the Prophet at the sun's decline and prayed noon with him; al-Ālūsī cites its transmission by Ibn Jarir, Ishaq, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r4.anchor: عن أبي مسعود عقبة بن عامر قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أتاني جبريل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r5.speaker: علي، ابن مسعود، زيد بن أسلم، النخعي، الضحاك، السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r5.claim: A second view takes dalūk as sunset, attributed to Ali, Ibn Masud, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Nakhai, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi, and chosen by al-Farra and Ibn Qutayba.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r5.anchor: وقيل لغروبها وهو المروي عندنا عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r6.speaker: ذو الرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r6.claim: Al-Farra cites Dhu al-Rummah's use of الدوالك to support the sunset sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r6.anchor: وأنشد لذي الرمة : مصابيح ليست باللواتي يقودها نجوم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r7.claim: The root دلك conveys transition, fitting both noon's movement from the meridian and sunset's movement below the horizon; sunset is a fuller transition because it changes both place and visibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r7.anchor: وأصل مادة د ل ك تدل على الانتقال ففي الزوال انتقال من دائرة نصف النهار إلى ما يليها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r8.claim: An alternative derives dalūk from ordinary rubbing: at noon a person looking at the sun rubs the eyes, making this derivation especially apt to the decline interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r8.anchor: وقيل إن الدلوك مصدر مزيد مأخوذ من المصدر المجرد أعني الدلك المعروف وهو أظهر في الزوال

ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds the noon interpretation strengthened because noon was the first daytime prayer performed on the Isra night and Gabriel began teaching the prayer at that time on the second day.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r9.anchor: أول صلاة صلاها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نهار ليلة الإسراء الظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r10.speaker: المبرد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r10.claim: Al-Mubarrad defines dalūk as the period from noon decline to sunset, making the command cover both noon and afternoon prayers; the other two views yield only one prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r10.anchor: وقال المبرد : دلوك الشمس من لدن زوالها إلى غروبها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r11.claim: The lām marks time and means after, as in Mutammim ibn Nuwayrah's elegy; it may also mean at, while al-Wahidi takes it causally because entry of the time causes prayer's obligation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r11.anchor: واللام للتأقيت متعلقة بأقم وهي بمعنى بعدكما في قول متمم بن نويرة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r12.claim: غسق الليل is the intensification of darkness and refers to the time of the night prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p131#3/r12.anchor: إلى شدة ظلمته كما قال الراغب وغيره وهو وقت العشاء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas defines غسق as night entering with darkness, citing Zuhayr's poetry; al-Nadr ibn Shumayl takes it as the beginning of night and cites a second poem, identifying it with sunset, as also reported from Mujahid.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له : أخبرني ما الغسق

ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r2.claim: The root suggests flowing: darkness pours onto the world as water flows from an eye.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r2.anchor: وأصله من السيلان يقال غسقت العين تغسق إذا هملت بالماء كان الظلمة تنصب على العالم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r3.speaker: جماعة من الشيعة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r3.claim: Some Shi'a extend غسق to both sunset and night prayer through dawn, and dalūk to noon and afternoon; including the endpoint yields all five prayer times and supports combining the paired prayers in residence without excuse.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r3.anchor: واختاره جماعة من الشيعة واستدلوا بها على أن وقت الظهر موسع إلى غروب الشمس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r4.speaker: عبيدة، زرارة عن أبي عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r4.claim: A report cited by al-Ayyashi says four prayers fall between noon and midnight: noon and afternoon before sunset, then sunset and night before midnight, each pair in order; al-Murtada adopts this timing.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r4.anchor: بما رواه العياشي باسناده عن عبيدة وزرارة عن أبي عبد الله أنه قال في هذه الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r5.claim: Most commentators instead identify dalūk with noon and غسق with the night prayer; the added mention of deep darkness supports this reading, and the verse requires each prayer at its appointed time, not continuous prayer throughout the span.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r5.anchor: والمعتمد عليه عند جمهور المفسرين أن دلوك الشمس وقت الظهر وغسق الليل وقت العشاء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r6.claim: The appointed prayer times are established by Gabriel's authentic teaching; the preposition phrase attaches to أقم, while Abu al-Baqa's alternative makes it a circumstantial phrase meaning prayer extended until night.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p132/r6.anchor: بل إقامة كل صلاة في وقتها الذي عين لها ببيان جبريل عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r1.claim: The time boundaries are given without listing gaps because people are awake through the successive daytime prayers, whereas sleep ordinarily separates night prayer from dawn; dawn is therefore singled out.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r1.anchor: لعل الاكتفاء ببيان المبدأ والمنتهى في أوقات الصلاة من غير فصل بينها لما أن الانسان فيما بين هذه الأوقات على اليقظة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r2.claim: The verse alone does not establish the Shi'i practice of combining noon with afternoon and sunset with night; without supporting reports it would more naturally allow all four together, an inference even Abu Ja'far rejected.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r2.anchor: فإنها إذا لم يضم إليها ذلك أولى بأن يستدل بها على جواز الجمع بين الأربعة جميعها لا بين الاثنتين والاثنتين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r3.claim: Some authentic reports do support their practice; Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet combined noon and afternoon and sunset and night in Medina without fear or travel, praying eight and seven units together.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r3.anchor: ما يؤيده ظواهر بعض الأحاديث الصحيحة كحديث ابن عباس وهو في صحيح مسلم صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r4.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r4.claim: One explanation attributes the combining to rain: al-Shafii's earlier view permits advancing or delaying the prayers, while his later view permits only advancing under stated conditions; Malik limits it to sunset and night prayers. Al-Ālūsī calls this weak because another Muslim report explicitly excludes rain.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r4.anchor: فمنهم من أوله بأنه جمع بعذر المطر والجمع بسبب ذلك تقديما وتأخيرا مذهب الشافعي في القديم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r5.claim: Another explanation says clouds obscured the times: the Prophet prayed noon, the clouds cleared, and afternoon time had begun; this could explain that pair but not sunset and night.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r5.anchor: ومنهم من أوله بأنه كان في غيم فصلى صلى الله عليه وسلم الظهر ثم انكشف الغيم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r6.claim: A third explanation says the first prayer was delayed to its final time and the second performed as its time began, creating only the appearance of combining; al-Ālūsī says this contradicts the plain report and cannot explain sunset and night.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r6.anchor: ومنهم من أوله بأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أخر الأولى وإلى آخر وقتها فصلاها فيه فلما فرغ منها دخل وقت الثانية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r7.speaker: أحمد، القاضي حسين، الخطابي، المتولي، الروياني
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r7.claim: A fourth view permits combining because of illness or similar hardship; this is the position of Ahmad and Qadi Husayn and was selected by several Shafii authorities.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133/r7.anchor: ومنهم من قال : هو محمول بالجمع بعذر المرض أو نحوه مما هو في معناه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r1.speaker: النووي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r1.claim: Al-Nawawi selects the illness interpretation; other jurists allow combining in residence for a need if it is not made habitual, including Ibn Sirin, Ashhab, al-Qaffal, Abu Ishaq al-Marwazi, hadith scholars, and Ibn al-Mundhir.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r1.anchor: وقال النووي : هو المختار في التأويل ومذهب جماعة من الأئمة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r2.claim: Asked why he combined, Ibn Abbas said the Prophet wanted not to burden anyone in his community; the report gives no illness as the cause and supports combining for need.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r2.anchor: ما صح عن ابن عباس ورواه مسلم أيضا أنه لما قال : جمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r3.speaker: الترمذي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r3.claim: Al-Tirmidhi claims only two hadiths in his collection were unanimously left unused, including Ibn Abbas's combining report and a report of killing a drinker on the fourth offense; al-Ālūsī says the first claim reflects inadequate research, while the second is sound because consensus establishes abrogation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r3.anchor: ويعلم مما ذكرنا من قول الترمذي في آخر كتابه ليس في كتابي حديث أجمعت الأمة على ترك العمل به إلا حديث ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r4.speaker: ابن الهمام
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Humam notes a counter-report in Muslim that sleep is not negligence, but negligence is staying awake until the next prayer's time begins; al-Ālūsī says the issue merits further discussion.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن الهمام : إن حديث ابن عباس معارض بما في مسلم من حديث التعريس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa forbids combining at either prayer's time except noon and afternoon at Arafat for the rite and sunset and night at Muzdalifa for the rite; al-Ālūsī says authentic reports do not support the restriction, though he favors the precaution of praying within undisputed times amid conflicting evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r5.anchor: وذهب الامام أبي حنيفة عدم جواز جمع صلاتي الظهر والعصر في وقت إحداهما والمغرب والعشاء كذلك مطلقا إلا بعرفات

ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r6.claim: Some take the commanded prayer as sunset alone and its beginning and end as the stated boundaries, arguing that sunset prayer lasts until twilight disappears; al-Ālūsī calls this contrary to Shafii's later position.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r6.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن المراد بالصلاة المأمور بإقامتها صلاة المغرب والتحديد المذكور بيان لمبدأ وقتها ومنتهاه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the detailed Shafii preparation period could exceed the interval from sunset to twilight; interpreting غسق as accumulated, intense darkness supports Abu Hanifa's view that night prayer begins when the white twilight after the red fades.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p133#2/r7.anchor: وفسر الغسق باجتماع الظلمة وشدتها كان ذلك مؤيدا لما في ظاهر الرواية عن الامام أبي حنيفة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r1.speaker: البيهقي، النووي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r1.claim: A prophetic report via Ibn Umar says twilight is redness and prayer becomes due when it vanishes; al-Bayhaqi and al-Nawawi say the sound version is only Ibn Umar's own statement, not a Prophetic report.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r1.anchor: قال البيهقي والنووي فيه الصحيح أنه موقوف عن ابن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r2.claim: Abu Hanifa sets afternoon prayer when an object's shadow reaches twice its height after subtracting the noon shadow; his two disciples set it at one object's height.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r2.anchor: فقال الإمام : هو إذا صار ظل كل شي مثليه بعد ظل الزوال

ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r3.speaker: المحققون
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r3.claim: Leading verifiers favor Abu Hanifa's afternoon timing; Ibn Nujaym says issuing a legal opinion against it is impermissible.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r3.anchor: بل قال ابن نجيم : إن الإفتاء بغيره لا يجوز

ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r4.claim: قرآن الفجر is coordinated with the object of أقم or is an accusative exhortation; most choose coordination and understand it as the dawn prayer, as reported from Ibn Abbas and Mujahid.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r4.anchor: والجمهور على الأول والمراد بقرآن الفجر صلاته كما روي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r5.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r5.claim: Al-Kashshaf argues that naming the dawn prayer Quran shows recitation is a pillar, opposing Ibn Ulayya and al-Asamm; its rebuttal says the naming may reflect recitation's recommended status, while al-Kashf defends the conventional whole-part relationship and al-Ālūsī notes objections to that defense.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r5.anchor: وسميت قرآنا أي قراءة لأنها ركنها كما سميت ركوعا وسجودا وهذه حجة على ابن علية والأضم في زعمهما

ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r6.speaker: الجصاص
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135/r6.claim: Al-Jassas keeps Quran literal and argues that the verse makes recitation obligatory in the dawn prayer, since أقم is a command and no other obligatory dawn recitation exists.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r1.speaker: الجصاص
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r1.claim: Al-Jassas rejects interpreting the phrase as the dawn prayer because it allegedly lacks evidence and the following tahajjud command cannot concern a dawn prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r1.anchor: وزعم أن كون المعنى صلوا الفجر غلط من وجهين الأول أنه صرف عن الحقيقة بغير دليل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī replies that أقم الصلاة is the familiar wording, and به in the next verse can refer back to Quran in its literal sense by an established usage; if dawn recitation is obligatory, other prayers follow by analogy.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r2.anchor: لاشتهار ( أقم الصلاة ) دون أقم القراءة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r3.claim: Some say naming the dawn prayer specifically as Quran hints that longer recitation is sought there than in other prayers.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r3.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن في التعبير عن صلاة الفجر بخصوصها بما ذكر إشارة إلى أنه يطلب فيها من تطويل القراءة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r4.claim: The Imam argues that linking Quran to dawn rules out praying at first light: because dawn begins with the darkness splitting, the command would require immediate prayer then; consensus rejects that obligation, leaving a recommendation against early darkness.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r4.anchor: وقال الإمام : إن في الآية دلالة على أنه ليس التغليس في صلاة الفجر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī says that inference fails because the dawn prayer is the same named prayer whether performed in darkness or later; authentic reports support praying in brighter light, including the Tirmidhi report that brighter dawn brings greater reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r5.anchor: لأن صلاة الفجر اسم للصلاة المخصوصة سواء وقعت بغلس أم أسفار والأخبار الصحيحة تدل على سنية الأسفار بها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r6.claim: An authentic Tahawi transmission from Ibrahim says the Companions were unanimous on praying in the later, brighter light; al-Ālūsī considers it implausible that they agreed against the Prophet's practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p135#2/r6.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال : ما اجتمع أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r1.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r1.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet prayed dawn in darkness; women wrapped in their cloaks attended and returned home unrecognized because of the darkness.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r1.anchor: وخبر عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي الصبح بغلس فتشهد معه نساء ملتفعات بمروطهن

ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects readings that limit the darkness to inside the mosque, since the report also says the women were unrecognized while returning home; he likewise finds a cloudy-day explanation unlikely because the wording suggests habitual practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r2.anchor: قولها : ثم يرجعن إلى بيوتهن ما يعرفهن أحد من الغلس إذ لا يمكن حمل هذا الغلس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r3.claim: The report is unlikely to be abrogated: abrogation needs an earlier practice, while Ibn Masud says he never saw the Prophet pray outside its time except the two prayers at Muzdalifa; some claim men's reports better capture congregational circumstances.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r3.anchor: وقيل هو منسوخ كما يدل عليه اجتماع الصحابة على التنوير ويبعد ذلك أن النسخ يقتضي سابقية وجود المنسوخ

ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r4.speaker: الطحاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r4.claim: Al-Tahawi recommends beginning dawn prayer in darkness and finishing in brighter light; al-Ālūsī says this conflicts with the jurists' description of the Hanafis' practice and with reports supporting their start and finish in brightness.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r4.anchor: وذكر الطحاوي أن الذي ينبغي الدخول في الفجر وقت التغليس والخروج وقت الأسفار

ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r5.claim: Although dawn prayer was one of the five imposed on the Isra night, the Prophet did not perform it the next morning because its manner had not yet been taught; noon was the first prayer taught, symbolizing his religion's eventual dominance.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r5.anchor: إلا أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يصلها صبح تلك الليلة لعدم العلم بكيفيتها حينئذ وإنما علم الكيفية بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r6.claim: Reports authenticated by Ahmad, al-Nasai, Ibn Majah, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Hakim say night and day angels witness dawn recitation; a soundayn report says they meet during the dawn prayer, and Abu Hurayra cites this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r6.anchor: أخرج أحمد والنسائي وابن ماجه والترمذي والحاكم وصححاه وجماعة عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال في تفسير ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r7.claim: These are the recording and guardian angels: day angels descend as night angels rise, meeting at dawn; the opposite exchange occurs at afternoon prayer according to reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r7.anchor: والمراد بهؤلاء الملائكة الكتبة والحفظة فتنزل ملائكة النهار وتصعد ملائكة الليل وتلتقي الطائفتان

ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r8.claim: The Imam's argument that a longer dawn prayer lets night angels witness it does not prove darkness is preferable: applied consistently, it would require delaying afternoon prayer until light disappears, which no one accepts.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p136/r8.anchor: وهذا مما يعكر على الإمام في زعمه أن هذا أيضا دليل قوي على أن التغليس أفضل من التنوير

ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r1.claim: Scholars dispute whether the same angelic group witnesses on successive days or different groups rotate; al-Ālūsī defers fuller discussion.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r1.anchor: وهل الطائفة التي تشهد اليوم مثلا تشهد غدا أو كل يوم تشهد طائفة أخرى لم تشهد قبل ولا تشهد بعد فيه خلاف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r2.claim: Other interpretations say dawn prayer is customarily witnessed by many worshipers or ought to be performed with a large congregation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r2.anchor: وقيل يشهد الكثير من المصلين في العادة وقيل من حقه أن تشهده الجماعة الكثيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r3.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r3.claim: The Imam proposes that the signs of divine power in the changing of light and darkness and waking from sleep, death's counterpart, are witnesses to dawn prayer; al-Ālūsī rejects restricting the phrase to this interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r3.anchor: وقيل تشهد وتحضر فيه شواهد القدرة من تبدل الضياء بالظلمة والانتباه بالنوم الذي هو أخو الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r4.claim: The verse encourages care for dawn prayer: the worshiper is accompanied by honored departing angels and welcomed by honored arrivals, and should be in the best state.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p137/r4.anchor: لأن العبد في ذلك الوقت مشيع كراما ومتلقى كراما فينبغي أن يكون على أحسن حال

ALUSI-FULL:v15p196#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p196#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p196#2/r5.claim: A mystical account distinguishes five prayers: communion at the hidden station, vision at the spirit, private converse at the secret, presence at the heart, and obedience at the soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p196#2/r5.anchor: وذكر أن الصلاة على خمسة أقسام صلاة المواصلة والمناغاة في مقام الخفي وصلاة المشاهدة في مقام الروح

ALUSI-FULL:v15p196#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p196#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p196#2/r6.claim: In this symbolism, the sun's decline marks unity's withdrawal from the servant's existence through annihilation; no prayer occurs at the zenith because the servant has no existence or self-awareness then.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p196#2/r6.anchor: فدلوك الشمس إشارة إلى زوال شمس الوحدة عن الاستواء على وجود العبد بالفناء المحض فإنه لا صلاة في حال الاستواء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p196#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p196#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p196#2/r7.claim: Prayer becomes due as the servant's shadow of existence appears, either while veiled from creation before union or while abiding after union.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p196#2/r7.anchor: وإنما تجب بالزوال وحدوث ظل وجود العبد سواء عند الاحتجاب بالخلق وهو حالة الفرق قبل الجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r1.claim: Nightfall symbolizes the darkening night of the lower self, while dawn recitation symbolizes the heart's dawn; dawn's Qur'an is witnessed by angels of night and day and signifies the heart's lights replacing traits of the self.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r1.anchor: وغسق الليل إشارة إلى غسق ليل النفس وقرآن الفجر إشارة إلى قرآن فجر القلب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r2.claim: The mystical ranking calls union the most subtle prayer, witnessing (asr) the best, secret prayer (maghrib) the lightest, the soul's prayer (isha) most stabilizing, and presence (fajr) most effective against Satan.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p197/r2.anchor: وأدل الصلوات وألطفها صلاة المواصلة وأفضلها صلاة الشهود المشار إليها بصلاة العصر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r1.claim: Ibn Masud says dulūk is sunset; Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi share this view.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r1.anchor: روي عن عبد الله بن مسعود أنه قال: الدلوك هو الغروب وهو قول إبراهيم النخعي ومقاتل بن حيان والضحاك والسدي.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عمر وجابر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, and Jabir say dulūk is the sun's decline at noon, as do Ata, Qatada, Mujahid, Hasan, and most Successors.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: وابن عمر وجابر: هو زوال الشمس وهو قول عطاء وقتادة ومجاهد والحسن وأكثر التابعين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r3.claim: The root sense is inclination, which can describe the sun's decline from zenith or its setting.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r3.anchor: ومعنى اللفظ يجمعهما لأن أصل الدلوك الميل والشمس تميل إذا زالت وغربت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r4.claim: He prefers the noon-decline interpretation because more scholars hold it and it makes the verse encompass all five prayers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r4.anchor: والحمل على الزوال أولى القولين لكثرة القائلين به ولأنا إذا حملناه عليه كانت الآية جامعة لمواقيت الصلاة كلها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r5.claim: On that reading, dulūk covers noon and afternoon prayers, darkness covers sunset and night prayers, and the dawn recitation is the morning prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114/r5.anchor: "فدلوك الشمس": يتناول صلاة الظهر والعصر و"إلى غسق الليل": يتناول المغرب والعشاء و"قرآن الفجر": هو صلاة الصبح

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r1.claim: Ghassaq means the appearance of darkness; Ibn Abbas says onset of night, Qatada the time of sunset prayer, and Mujahid sunset.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r1.anchor: {إلى غسق الليل} أي: ظهور ظلمته وقال ابن عباس: بدو الليل وقال قتادة: وقت صلاة المغرب وقال مجاهد: غروب الشمس.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r2.claim: Qurʾān al-fajr means dawn prayer, called Qur'an because the prayer is not valid without recitation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r2.anchor: {وقرآن الفجر} يعني: صلاة الفجر سمى صلاة الفجر قرآنا لأنها لا تجوز إلا بقرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r3.claim: Al-Farra construes the accusative “Qur'an” as coordinated with prayer: establish the dawn recitation/prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما: أنه عطف على الصلاة أي: وأقم قرآن الفجر قاله الفراء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r4.speaker: أهل البصرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r4.claim: The Basrans construe it as exhortation: dawn recitation is incumbent on you.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r4.anchor: وقال أهل البصرة: على الإغراء أي وعليك قرآن الفجر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r5.claim: The dawn prayer is witnessed by both the night angels and the day angels.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r5.anchor: أي: يشهده ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r6.claim: The Prophet says congregational prayer surpasses an individual's prayer by twenty-five portions, and the night and day angels gather at dawn; Abu Hurayra cites this verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p114#2/r6.anchor: تفضل صلاة الجميع على صلاة أحدكم وحده بخمس وعشرين جزءا وتجتمع ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار في صلاة الفجر

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r1.claim: Duluk means the sun's decline, supported by Gabriel's report that he prayed the noon prayer with the Prophet at that moment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r1.anchor: لدلوك الشمس } لزوالها ويدل عليه قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r2.claim: Another view takes duluk as sunset; the root suggests transition, as do related forms such as dalaj, dalah, dalaʿ, dalaf, and dalah.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r2.anchor: وقيل لغروبها وأصل التركيب للانتقال ومنه الدلك فإن الدلك لا تستقر يده،

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r3.claim: A further derivation is eye-rubbing to ward off the sun's rays; the lām in duluk is feminine, like that in لثلاث خلون.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r3.anchor: وقيل الدلوك من الدلك لأن الناظر إليها يدلك عينيه ليدفع شعاعها، واللام للتأنيث مثلها في: لثلاث خلون

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r4.claim: The end of nightfall is its darkness, the time of the final night prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r4.anchor: غسق الليل } إلى ظلمته وهو وقت صلاة العشاء الأخيرة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r5.claim: The 'Qur'an of dawn' means the morning prayer, named for its recitation as its pillar, like naming it by bowing or prostration.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r5.anchor: وقرءان الفجر } وصلاة الصبح، سميت قرآنا لأنه ركنها كما سميت ركوعا وسجودا،

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r6.claim: The verse does not establish the obligation of recitation in the dawn prayer if 'Qur'an' is a metaphor for the prayer, since the recitation could be recommended; if it means recitation, the command obliges it in dawn and by analogy in other prayers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r6.anchor: واستدل به على وجوب القراءة فيها ولا دليل فيه لجواز أن يكون التجوز لكونها مندوبة فيها،

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r7.claim: The dawn prayer is witnessed by night and day angels, or by signs of power in dawn and waking from sleep, or by its many worshippers, or it is a prayer fitting a large congregation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r7.anchor: تشهده ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار، أو شواهد القدرة من تبدل الظلمة بالضياء والنوم الذي هو أخو الموت بالانتباه أو كثير من المصلين

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r8.claim: If duluk is decline, the verse encompasses all five prayers; if it is sunset, it covers night prayers only. Another view makes it the Maghrib prayer and uses the phrase as its time's beginning and end, extending it to disappearance of twilight.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:78/r8.anchor: والآية جامعة للصلوات الخمس إن فسر الدلوك بالزوال ولصلوات الليل وحدها إن فسر بالغروب. وقيل المراد بالصلاة صلاة المغرب وقوله { لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق اليل } بيان لمبدأ الوقت ومنتهاه،

QASHANI:17:75/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:75/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:75/r3.claim: Prayer has five inward forms and stations: intimate communion in hiddenness, witnessing in spirit, confidential converse in the secret, presence in the heart, and compliant submission in the self.
QASHANI:17:75/r3.anchor: اعلم أن الصلاة على خمسة أقسام

QASHANI:17:75/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:75/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:75/r4.claim: The sun's decline marks unity's withdrawal from the servant's existence after annihilation; no prayer is possible at complete annihilation because prayer requires a praying servant.
QASHANI:17:75/r4.anchor: فدلوك الشمس هو علامة زوال شمس الوحدة عن الاستواء على وجود العبد بالفناء المحض

QASHANI:17:75/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:75/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:75/r5.claim: At decline, the servant's shadow or existence returns, whether veiled by creation before union or abiding after union; prayer then continues until the self's night and the heart's dawn.
QASHANI:17:75/r5.anchor: إذا حدث ظل وجود العبد سواء عند الاحتجاب بالخلق حالة الفرق قبل الجمع

QASHANI:17:75/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:75/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:75/r6.claim: The gentlest prayer is intimate communion; the most excellent is the spirit's witnessing, identified with the middle prayer and interpreted as the afternoon prayer.
QASHANI:17:75/r6.anchor: وأفضلها وأشرفها صلاة الشهود للروح المشار إليها بصلاة العصر

QASHANI:17:75/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:75/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:75/r7.claim: The secret's confidential prayer is the brief sunset interval when the heart first appears behind a veil; the short interval explains the recommendation to shorten sunset recitation.
QASHANI:17:75/r7.anchor: وأوحاها وأخفها صلاة السر بالمناجاة أول وقت الاحتجاب بظهور القلب

QASHANI:17:75/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:75/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:75/r8.claim: Dawn recitation is the heart's presence, during disclosure of attributes and unveilings; congregation and longer recitation are especially recommended then, when night and day angels attend.
QASHANI:17:75/r8.anchor: فإنها في وقت تجليات أنوار الصفات ونزول المكاشفات ولهذا استحب التكثر في جماعة صلاة الصبح

QASHANI:17:75/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:75/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:75/r9.claim: The dawn prayer signals the heart's qualities and light descending as the self's qualities recede; it is witnessed because angels of night and day are present.
QASHANI:17:75/r9.anchor: محضورا بحضور ملائكة الليل والنهار إشارة إلى نزول صفات القلب وأنوارها

QASHANI:17:75/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:75/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:75/r10.claim: The night prayer most firmly tames the self, so silence after it until sleep is prescribed except for remembrance; loud prayer rebukes Satan where he can whisper, while the spirit's hidden station calls for quiet.
QASHANI:17:75/r10.anchor: سن فيما جعل آية لها من صلاة العشاء السكوت بعدها حتى النوم إلا بذكر الله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r4.claim: Prayer should be fully established with all its conditions, pillars, preliminaries, and ends; it is the core of worship and intimate communion with God.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r4.anchor: بفعل جميع شرائطها وأركانها ومبادئها وغاياتها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r5.claim: Prayer is a great aid against enemies and hardship and a cause of well-being; the Prophet turned to prayer when distressed.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r5.anchor: أن الصلاة أعظم ناصر على الأعداء الذين يريدون بمكرهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r6.claim: Duluk is glossed as setting, yellowing, declining, or passing the meridian; using the term across its senses covers noon, afternoon, and sunset prayers.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r6.anchor: قال في القاموس : دلكت الشمس : غربت أو اصفرت أو مالت أو زالت

BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r7.claim: The term also indicates that sunset prayer lasts until the twilight disappears; waiting for each time already counts as being in prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p414/r7.anchor: لأن الإنسان في صلاة ما كان ينتظر الصلاة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r1.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r1.claim: Al-Razi defines ghassaq as the night’s darkness becoming fully established.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r1.anchor: وقال الرازي في اللوامع : وهو استحكام ظلمة الليل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r2.speaker: الرماني
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r2.claim: Al-Rummani instead glosses ghassaq as the appearance of night’s darkness.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r3.claim: “Qur’an of dawn” refers to the dawn prayer, whose long, audible recitation distinguishes it from the afternoon prayer and encourages people despite sleep.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r3.anchor: عبر عنها بالقرآن لأنه مع كونه أعظم أركان الصلاة يطول فيها القراءة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r4.claim: The phrase may also be parsed as an accusative exhortation to perform the dawn recitation.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r4.anchor: وقيل : نصب على الإغراءن وكأنه عبر عنها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r5.claim: The dawn recitation is witnessed by the night and day angel groups and delights hearing, heart, and spirit.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r5.anchor: يشهده فريقا الملائكة , وهو أهل لأن يشهده كل أحد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that congregational prayer exceeds solitary prayer by twenty-five degrees and that night and day angels meet at dawn; he cites this verse.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : فضل صلاة الجميع على صلاة الواحد خمس وعشرون درجة , وتجتمع ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r7.claim: The commentators infer from the report that prayer is due at the beginning of its time and that praying dawn in the darkness before daybreak is preferable.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p415/r7.anchor: قالوا : وهذا دليل على وجوب الصلاة بأول الوقت , وأن التغليس بصلاة الفجر أفضل

DURR-FULL:v5p320/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r3.claim: Ibn Masud says duluk means sunset, as Arabs say that the sun has dipped when it sets.
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r3.anchor:
عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: دلوك الشمس: غروبها
تقول العرب: إذا غربت الشمس: دلكت الشمس

DURR-FULL:v5p320/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r4.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r4.claim: Ali also says duluk means sunset.
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r4.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: دلوكها غروبها

DURR-FULL:v5p320/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r5.claim: A report from the Prophet interprets duluk as the sun's decline from its zenith.
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r5.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله: {أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس} قال: لزوال الشمس

DURR-FULL:v5p320/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r6.claim: Ibn Umar also interprets duluk as the sun's decline from zenith; the report is explicitly graded weak.
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r6.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال: {لدلوك الشمس} زوالها

DURR-FULL:v5p320/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r7.claim: Ibn Umar calls duluk the sun's movement after midday.
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r7.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال: {لدلوك الشمس} زياغها بعد نصف النهار

DURR-FULL:v5p320/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says duluk is the sun's decline, when the shadow returns or lengthens.
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: دلوكها زوالها

DURR-FULL:v5p320/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r9.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Gabriel came at the sun's decline, prayed noon prayer with the Prophet, and thereby explained the timing.
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r9.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أتاني جبريل عليه السلام لدلوك الشمس حين زالت

DURR-FULL:v5p320/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r10.speaker: أبو برزة الأسلمي
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r10.claim: Abu Barza says the Prophet prayed noon when the sun declined and recited this verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r10.anchor: عن أبي برزة الأسلمي رضي الله عنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي الظهر إذا زالت الشمس ثم تلا

DURR-FULL:v5p320/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r11.claim: Mujahid says his master Qays ibn al-Saib waited for the sun's decline before praying noon.
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه قال: كنت أقود مولاي قيس بن السائب فيقول لي: أدلكت الشمس

DURR-FULL:v5p320/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r12.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r12.claim: Anas says the Prophet prayed noon at the sun's decline.
DURR-FULL:v5p320/r12.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي الظهر عند دلوك الشمس

DURR-FULL:v5p321/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r1.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the darkness of night as the final evening prayer.
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه في قوله: {إلى غسق الليل} قال: العشاء الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v5p321/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas defines nightfall as the gathering darkness of night.
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: {غسق الليل} اجتماع الليل وظلمته

DURR-FULL:v5p321/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r3.claim: Ibn Masud also defines it as the onset of night.
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: {غسق الليل} بدو الليل

DURR-FULL:v5p321/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas tells Nafi ibn al-Azraq that ghassaq means the onset of night with darkness, citing Zuhayr's line about darkness descending.
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله: {إلى غسق الليل

DURR-FULL:v5p321/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r5.claim: Mujahid says duluk is when the sun declines and ghassaq is sunset.
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه قال: {لدلوك الشمس} حين تزيغ و {غسق الليل} غروب الشمس

DURR-FULL:v5p321/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra says duluk is the sun's decline from the middle of the sky and ghassaq is sunset.
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: {لدلوك الشمس} إذا زالت عن بطن السماء و {غسق الليل} غروب الشمس

DURR-FULL:v5p321/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Quran at dawn as the morning prayer.
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {وقرآن الفجر} قال: صلاة الصبح

DURR-FULL:v5p321/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r8.claim: Mujahid likewise identifies Quran at dawn as the dawn prayer.
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {وقرآن الفجر} قال: صلاة الفجر

DURR-FULL:v5p321/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r9.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r9.claim: Ata says angels and jinn witness the dawn recitation.
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r9.anchor: عن عطاء رضي الله عنه في قوله: {إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا} قال: تشهده الملائكة والجن

DURR-FULL:v5p321/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r10.claim: Abu Hurayra says the angels of night and day gather for the dawn prayer and witness its recitation.
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r10.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا} قال: تشهده ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

DURR-FULL:v5p321/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r11.claim: The Prophet says night and day angels meet at dawn prayer; Abu Hurayra supports this by reciting the verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r11.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: تجتمع ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار في صلاة الفجر

DURR-FULL:v5p321/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r12.claim: Ibn Masud says the angels guarding night and day meet at dawn prayer, when both groups descend.
DURR-FULL:v5p321/r12.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: يتدارك الحرسان من ملائكة الله تعالى حارس الليل وحارس النهار عند صلاة الصبح

DURR-FULL:v5p323/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p323/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p323/r1.claim: The dawn recitation is witnessed by God and the angels of night and day.
DURR-FULL:v5p323/r1.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه قال: قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: {إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا} قال: يشهده الله وملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

DURR-FULL:v5p323/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p323/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p323/r2.claim: The angels of night and day witness the dawn recitation.
DURR-FULL:v5p323/r2.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا} قال: تشهده ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

DURR-FULL:v5p323/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p323/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p323/r3.claim: Ibn Masud told worshippers seated with their backs to the qibla to move away so they would not obstruct the angels' prayer; he called the two dawn units the angels' prayer.
DURR-FULL:v5p323/r3.anchor: دخل عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه المسجد لصلاة الفجر فإذا قوم قد أسندوا ظهورهم إلى القبلة فقال: نحوا عن القبلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r1.claim: The five daily prayers were prescribed on the Night Journey by a sound hadith, but this schedule later clarified prayer times after the obligation had been established and communicated to the Companions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r1.anchor: كان شرع الصلوات الخمس للأمة ليلة الإسراء ، كما ثبت في الحديث الصحيح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r2.claim: The verse gathers the prayer legislation given around the Night Journey and begins a fresh passage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r2.anchor: فلذلك جاءت هذه الآية في هذه السورة التي نزلت عقب حادث الإسراء جمعا للتشريع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r3.claim: After granting protection and victory, God commands gratitude through prayer and additional worship, which prepares for the promised praised station.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r3.anchor: أن الله لما امتن على النبي بالعصمة وبالنصر ذكره بشكر النعمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r4.claim: Though the command addresses the Prophet, Quranic legislative address to him normally includes his community unless evidence indicates exclusive application; Muslims understood this convention.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r4.anchor: أن خطاب النبي بتشريعع تدخل فيه أمته إلا إذا دل دليل على اختصاصه بذلك الحكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r5.claim: إقامة prayer is figurative for persistent, regular observance; لام in لدلوك marks timing and means عند.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r5.anchor: والإقامة : مجاز في المواظبة والإدامة . وقد تقدم عند قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r6.claim: دلوك has three attested senses: the sun’s passage from its midday zenith, its later movement toward the afternoon, or its setting, making it a shared term.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r6.anchor: فصار لفظ الدلوك مشتركا في المعاني الثلاثة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r7.claim: غسق is darkness at the disappearance of the twilight glow, the time of the evening prayer, also called العتمة.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p181/r7.anchor: والغسق : الظلمة ، وهي انقطاع بقايا شعاع الشمس حين يماثل سواد أفق الغروب

SULAMI:v1p393#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p393#4/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p393#4/r1.claim: Some say standing in worship during the pre-dawn hours is witnessed by the worshiper and bears witness against them.
SULAMI:v1p393#4/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : القيام في أوقات الأسحار مشهود من صاحبه وشاهد عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r4.claim: Exegetes agree the command to establish prayer refers to obligatory prayers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r4.anchor: هذه بإجماع من المفسرين إشارة إلى الصلوات المفروضة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r5.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس وأبو بردة والحسن والجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r5.claim: They read sun decline as noon, covering noon and afternoon; darkness covers evening and night; dawn recitation is morning prayer, so all prayers are covered.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r5.anchor: فقال ابن عمر وابن عباس وأبو بردة والحسن والجمهور: «دلوك الشمس» زوالها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports Gabriel came at sun decline and led the Prophet in noon prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r6.anchor: وروى ابن مسعود أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أتاني جبريل لدلوك الشمس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r7.speaker: جابر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r7.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet told Abu Bakr to go after the sun had declined, identifying that time as dulk.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r7.anchor: وروى جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج من عنده وقد طعم وزالت الشمس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r8.claim: They take sun decline as sunset, night darkness as ʿIsha, and dawn recitation as morning prayer, leaving noon and afternoon unmentioned.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p476#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود وابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r1.claim: The first reading is preferable because it covers all prayers; both are linguistically valid since dulk is the sun’s slant from noon to sunset.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r1.anchor: والقول الأول أصوب لعمومه الصلوات، وهما من جهة اللغة حسنان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r2.claim: An Arab used yudālik for leaning toward delay in repayment; poems illustrate the sun’s slant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r2.anchor: ومن الدلوك الذي هو الميل قول الأعرابي للحسن بن أبي الحسن أيدالك الرجل امرأته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأصمعي وأبو عمرو الشيباني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r3.claim: They explain bi-rāḥ in poetry as the sun’s rays, shaded with the observer’s palm to see its angle.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة الأصمعي وأبو عمرو الشيباني ومعناه براحة الناظر يستكف بها أبدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud reportedly explains dakat bi-rāḥ as a place called Barāḥ; Ibn ʿAṭiyya accepts this if truly transmitted from him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r4.anchor: وذكر الطبري عن ابن مسعود أنه قال: دلكت براح يعني براح مكانا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r5.claim: Ghasaq means darkness gathering and thickening; Ibn Abbas says it begins at nightfall.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: غسق الليل بدؤه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r6.claim: Qurʾān of dawn may take an implicit recite, coordinate with prayer, or be exhortative; morning prayer is named for its long, audible recitation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r6.anchor: ونصب قوله وقرآن بفعل مضمر تقديره واقرأ قرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r7.claim: Dawn is witnessed by angels of night and day, as in the report that they meet at dawn and afternoon prayers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r7.anchor: وقوله إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا معناه ليشهده حفظة النهار وحفظة الليل من الملائكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r8.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r8.claim: A famous report says night and day angels alternate and meet at dawn and afternoon prayers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r8.anchor: يتعاقبون فيكم ملائكة بالليل وملائكة بالنهار، ويجتمعون في صلاة الصبح وصلاة العصر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r9.speaker: محمد بن سهل بن عسكر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r9.claim: Al-Tabari reports via Abu al-Darda that Ibn ʿAskar says God and angels witness; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the report weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p477/r9.anchor: قال محمد بن سهل بن عسكر يشهده الله وملائكته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r1.claim: Aqim al-ṣalāh means perform the prayer at the sun’s decline.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى أقم الصلاة أي أدها لدلوك الشمس أي عند دلوكها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r2.claim: The lām in li-dulūk may mean “at/in.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r2.anchor: وذكر أبن الأنباري في اللام قولين أحدهما أنها بمعنى في

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the lām is emphatic, as in 27:72.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r3.anchor: والثاني أنها مؤكدة كقوله ردف لكم النمل 72

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r4.claim: Dulūk extends from the sun’s noon decline until it sets.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة دلوكها من عند زوالها إلى أن تغيب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r5.claim: Dulūk can mean the sun’s tilt at noon or its tilt toward setting.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r5.anchor: وقال الزجاج ميلها وقت الظهيرة دلوك وميلها للغروب دلوك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r6.speaker: الأزهري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r6.claim: Dulūk means decline; the sun is called dālik when it declines at noon or sets because in either case it has left its position.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r6.anchor: وقال الأزهري معنى الدلوك في كلام العرب الزوال ولذلك قيل للشمس إذا زالت نصف النهار دالكة وإذا أفلت دالكة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r7.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r7.claim: A report about a meal with the Prophet says he left after noon and identified that time as the sun’s dulūk.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r7.anchor: روى جابر بن عبد الله قال دعوت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن شاء من اصحابه فطعموا عندي ثم خرجوا حين زالت الشمس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r8.speaker: ابن عمر وأبو برزة وأبو هريرة والحسن والشعبي وسعيد بن جبير وأبو العالية ومجاهد وعطاء وعبيد بن عمير وقتادة والضحاك ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r8.claim: The first interpretation takes dulūk as the sun’s noon decline.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r8.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عمر وأبي برزة وأبي هريرة والحسن والشعبي وسعيد بن جبير وأبي العالية ومجاهد وعطاء وعبيد بن عمير وقتادة والضحاك ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r9.speaker: الأزهري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r9.claim: The noon-decline interpretation includes all five prayers: noon and afternoon, the two night prayers, then dawn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r9.anchor: قال الأزهري لتكون الآية جامعة للصلوات الخمس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود والنخعي وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r10.claim: The second interpretation takes dulūk as sunset.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r10.anchor: والثاني أنه غروبها قاله ابن مسعود والنخعي وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r11.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r11.claim: The Arabs whom al-Farrāʾ observed used dulūk for the sun’s disappearance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r11.anchor: قال الفراء ورأيت العرب تذهب في الدلوك إلى غيبوبة الشمس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r12.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r12.claim: Ibn Qutayba prefers sunset because Arabs say a star has dalaka when it sets; he cites Dhū al-Rumma.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r12.anchor: وهذا اختيار ابن قتيبة قال لأن العرب تقول دلك النجم اذا غاب قال ذو الرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r13.claim: A line about the sun being ill and pushed by the palm refers to the sun nearing sunset and viewed under a shielding hand.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r13.anchor: والشمس قد كادت تكون دنفا … أدفعها بالراح كي تزحلفا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r14.claim: On the sunset interpretation, the prayer at dulūk is Maghrib and ghasaq means darkness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p71#2/r14.anchor: فعلى هذا المراد بهذه الصلاة المغرب فأما غسق الليل فظلامه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r1.claim: The prayer associated with the onset of night’s darkness is ʿIshāʾ.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r2.claim: The prayer associated with the onset of night’s darkness is Maghrib.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r3.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r3.claim: If ghasaq means Maghrib, the verse may specify its time from sunset until darkness begins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r3.anchor: قال القاضي أبو يعلى فيحتمل ان يكون المراد بيان وقت المغرب انه من غروب الشمس إلى غسق الليل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r4.claim: The prayer associated with ghasaq includes both Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r5.claim: Qurʾān al-fajr means recitation at dawn, namely the dawn prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى وقرآن الفجر المعنى وأقم قراءة الفجر قال المفسرون المراد به صلاة الفجر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r6.claim: Calling prayer “Quran” shows that prayer includes recitation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج وفي هذا فائدة عظيمة تدل على أن الصلاة لا تكون إلا بقراءة حين سميت الصلاة قرآنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r7.claim: The Prophet said that the night and day angels witness the dawn recitation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p73/r7.anchor: روى أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال تشهده ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود ومجاهد وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r1.claim: They interpret the sun's dulūk as its setting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r1.anchor: قيل (8) لغروبها. قاله ابن مسعود، ومجاهد، وابن زيد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r2.claim: He interprets dulūk as the sun's decline from its zenith; Ibn Umar also transmits this, as do Abu Barza and several others.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers the zenith-decline interpretation, adducing Jabir's report that the Prophet left after the sun declined and called it the time of dulūk.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r3.anchor: وبه قال الحسن، والضحاك، وأبو جعفر الباقر، وقتادة. واختاره ابن جرير،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r4.claim: On the preferred reading, the interval from the sun's decline to night darkness covers the five obligatory prayers, while Qur'an at dawn means Fajr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r4.anchor: فعلى هذا تكون هذه الآية دخل فيها أوقات الصلاة الخمسة فمن قوله: {لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r5.claim: The Prophet's sayings and actions establish the detailed prayer times through continuous, mass-transmitted practice among Muslims.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p101#2/r5.anchor: وقد ثبتت السنة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تواترا من أفعاله وأقواله (2)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ابن مسعود وأبي هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r1.claim: Fajr is witnessed by both the night and day angels.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r2.claim: Congregational prayer is twenty-five times more meritorious than praying alone, and night and day angels gather for Fajr; Abu Hurayra connects this with the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r2.anchor: قال: "فضل صلاة الجميع على صلاة الواحد خمس وعشرون درجة، وتجتمع ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار في صلاة الفجر".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r3.claim: Night and day angels alternate among people and meet at Fajr and ʿAṣr; departing angels report that they left the servants praying.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r3.anchor: يتعاقبون فيكم ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار (8) ، ويجتمعون في صلاة الصبح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود وإبراهيم النخعي ومجاهد وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r4.claim: They say the two angelic watches meet at Fajr, one group ascending while the other remains.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r4.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود: يجتمع الحرسان (10) في صلاة الفجر، فيصعد هؤلاء ويقيم هؤلاء.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r5.claim: A report of the divine descent says God invites those seeking forgiveness, asking, or praying until dawn; the verse is then linked to God's and both angel groups' witnessing Fajr. Ibn Kathir notes this route is unique to Ziyada.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p102/r5.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فذكر حديث النزول وأنه تعالى يقول: "من يستغفرني أغفر له،

JISHUMI:v6p4277/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r3.claim: Duluk can mean sunset or the sun's decline; its root is rubbing, since people rub their eyes against the rays when the sun declines or sets.
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r3.anchor: الدلوك: قيل: الغروب، وقيل: الزوال، وأصله من الدلك

JISHUMI:v6p4277/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r4.claim: Ibn Umar glosses duluk as the sun's inclination; Tha'lab likewise says the sun has declined and cites poetry for the time and the act of shading one's eyes.
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r4.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر الدلوك: الميل. قال ثعلب: دلكت الشمس مالت

JISHUMI:v6p4277/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r5.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r5.claim: The line uses dalak for the time when the sun declines.
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r5.anchor: وأنشد: تعرض الزهراء في وقت الدلك وقال آخر: هذا مقام قدمي رباح

JISHUMI:v6p4277/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r6.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r6.claim: The second line witnesses the sun's inclination; barāḥ can name the sun or the hand shielding the eyes from its light.
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r6.anchor: أي: مالت، روي براح بفتح الباء، جعله اسما للشمس

JISHUMI:v6p4277/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r7.claim: Ghassaq means darkness; the poet uses it for night growing dark.
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r7.anchor: والغسق: الظلام، غسق يغسق غسوقا، قال الشاعر: أمن هذا الليل إذا غسقا

JISHUMI:v6p4277/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r11.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r11.claim: Qur'an al-Fajr is accusative by coordination with prayer; al-Akhfash disallows coordination with nightfall, while another view makes it an exhortation to attend to dawn recitation.
JISHUMI:v6p4277/r11.anchor: نصب قرآن الفجر عطفا على الصلاة، كأنه قيل: أقم الصلاة وقرآن الفجر، عن الفراء

JISHUMI:v6p4279/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r5.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r5.claim: The command to establish prayer addresses the Prophet for himself and others, or a human listener, his community, or himself personally.
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r5.anchor: قيل: خطاب للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - والمراد هو وغيره

JISHUMI:v6p4279/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r6.claim: To establish prayer means to perform it fully.

JISHUMI:v6p4279/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r7.speaker: إبراهيم، ومقاتل، والضحاك، والسدي، وابن زيد
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r7.claim: These authorities take the sun's duluk to mean sunset, making the prayer in view the Maghrib prayer according to Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Zayd.
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r7.anchor: قيل: غروبها، عن إبراهيم، ومقاتل، والضحاك، والسدي، وابن زيد.

JISHUMI:v6p4279/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r8.speaker: ابن عباس، وابن عمر، وجابر، وأبو العالية، وعطاء، وقتادة، ومجاهد، والحسن، ومقاتل، وجعفر بن محمد، وعبيد بن حجر
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r8.claim: These authorities take duluk as the sun's decline; this is also reported from the Prophet, and prayer then runs from noon decline until nightfall.
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r8.anchor: قيل: دلوكها زوالها، عن ابن عباس بخلاف، وابن عمر، وجابر، وأبي العالية

JISHUMI:v6p4279/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r9.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r9.claim: Ghassaq is the appearance of darkness; Ibn Abbas and Qatada call it the start of night, Mujahid sunset, and Abu Ubayda the blackness of night.
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r9.anchor: قيل: ظهور ظلامه، عن أبي علي. وقيل: هو بدو الليل، عن ابن عباس، وقتادة

JISHUMI:v6p4279/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r10.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r10.claim: Hasan distributes prayer times as noon and afternoon at the sun's decline, then sunset and night prayers until nightfall; Qur'an al-Fajr is the dawn prayer.
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r10.anchor: فقيل: أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس أي: الظهر والعصر إلى غسق الليل أي: المغرب والعشاء، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v6p4279/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r11.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r11.claim: The dawn prayer is called Qur'an because recitation is emphasized in it; alternatively the phrase names what is recited in that prayer.
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r11.anchor: سمي قرآنا لتأكيد القراءة في الصلاة، عن الزجاج.

JISHUMI:v6p4279/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r12.speaker: ابن عباس، وقتادة، وابن زيد، وإبراهيم، ومجاهد
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r12.claim: Dawn recitation is witnessed by the angels of night and day; a report from Ali identifies it as the middle prayer and says it is written in both registers, with angels arriving and departing while worshippers pray.
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r12.anchor: قيل: تشهده ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار، عن ابن عباس، وقتادة، وابن زيد

JISHUMI:v6p4279/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r13.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r13.claim: Being witnessed can mean that mosques should witness the prayer by having it performed communally.
JISHUMI:v6p4279/r13.anchor: وقيل: شهود أن من حقها أن تشهد المساجد لها، وتقام بالجماعة. عن أبي مسلم.

AKHFASH:v2p426/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p426/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p426/r1.claim: وقرآن الفجر is elliptical for an instruction that dawn recitation is also incumbent on you.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r1.claim: Duluk may mean sunset or, alternatively, the sun's decline from its zenith; the word is derived from rubbing because one rubs the eye when looking toward the sun.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r2.claim: Gabriel came at the sun's decline and prayed the noon prayer with the Prophet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r2.anchor: أتاني جبريل عليه السلام لدلوك الشمس حين زالت الشمس . فصلى بي الظهر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r3.claim: If duluk means zenith, the verse covers all five prayers; if it means sunset, noon and afternoon prayers fall outside its span.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r3.anchor: فإن كان الدلوك الزوال فالآية جامعة للصلوات الخمس ، وإن كان الغروب فقد خرجت منها الظهر والعصر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r4.claim: Ghasaq means darkness and marks the time of the night prayer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r4.anchor: والغسق : الظلمة ، وهو وقت صلاة العشاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r5.claim: Qur'an al-fajr denotes the dawn prayer, naming it for its recitation because recitation is a pillar, like bowing, prostration, and qunūt; this refutes Ibn ʿUlayya and al-Aṣamm's denial that recitation is a pillar.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r5.anchor: سميت قرآنا وهو القراءة ، لأنها ركن ، كما سميت ركوعا وسجودا وقنوتا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r6.claim: The dawn prayer is witnessed by the angels of night and day, as one group descends while the other ascends; alternatively, many worshippers witness it, or it should be attended by a large congregation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r6.anchor: يشهده ملائكة الليل والنهار ، ينزل هؤلاء ، ويصعد هؤلاء ؛ فهو في آخر ديوان الليل وأول ديوان النهار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r7.claim: The verse may urge lengthy dawn recitation so people hear the Qur'an and its reward increases; dawn is accordingly the longest prayer in recitation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p641/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { أقم الصلواة } حثا على طول القراءة في صلاة الفجر ، لكونها مكثورا عليها ، ليسمع الناس القرآن فيكثر الثواب

FARRA:v2p128/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p128/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
FARRA:v2p128/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says دلوك is the sun’s decline from its zenith at noon.
FARRA:v2p128/r4.anchor: جاء عن ابن عباس قال: هو زيغوغتها وزوالها للظهر.

FARRA:v2p128/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p128/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p128/r5.claim: Farra says he heard Arabs use دلوك for sunset; a poem’s براح means the sun had set, with the speaker checking the sun’s disappearance by hand.
FARRA:v2p128/r5.anchor: حتى دلكت براح يعني الساقي ذبب

FARRA:v2p129/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p129/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p129/r1.claim: غسق الليل is the onset of darkness at the evening and night prayers.

FARRA:v2p129/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p129/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p129/r2.claim: قرآن الفجر means the dawn prayer, witnessed by the angels of night and day.
FARRA:v2p129/r2.anchor: يعني صلاة الفجر تشهدها ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r1.claim: Dulūk means sunset, so the commanded prayer is Maghrib; Mujahid transmitted this from Ibn Abbas and it is Abu Hanifa's school.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أنه غروبها , وأن الصلاة المأمور بها صلاة المغرب , ومنه قول ذي الرمة :

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r2.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية الشعبي عنه وأبو بردة والحسن وقتادة ومجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r2.claim: Dulūk may mean the sun's decline from its zenith, making the prayer Dhuhr; this is the view of al-Shafiʿi and Malik, supported by a report of Gabriel praying Dhuhr with the Prophet at decline.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنه زوالها , والصلاة المأمور بها صلاة الظهر , وهذا قول ابن عباس في رواية الشعبي عنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r3.claim: For sunset, a person rubs the eyes with a palm to see the setting sun; for decline, its strong rays make one rub one's eyes.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r3.anchor: يدلك عينيه براحته لتبينها , ومن جعله اسما لزوالها فلأنه يدلك عينيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r4.speaker: author
