MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r4.claim: The basic lexical sense of dulūk is inclination, applicable to the sun at both decline and sunset.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r4.anchor: وقيل إن أصل الدلوك في اللغة هو الميل , والشمس تميل عند زوالها وغروبها فلذلك انطلق على كل واحد منهما .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r5.speaker: الفراء وابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r5.claim: Ghasaq is the onset or appearance of darkness, supported by Zuhayr's line about darkness falling.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r5.anchor: أحدهما : أنه ظهور ظلامه , قاله الفراء وابن عيسى , ومنه قول زهير :

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r6.claim: Ghasaq can mean night drawing near and arriving.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p262/r6.anchor: الثاني : أنه دنو الليل وإقباله , وهوقول ابن عباس وقتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r1.claim: The prayer at the time described by dulūk and ghasaq may be Maghrib.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أنها صلاة المغرب , وهو قول ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر الطبري
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r2.claim: Alternatively, it may be the night prayer, ʿIshāʾ.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r2.anchor: صلاة العشاء الآخرة , قاله أبو جعفر الطبري . ثم قال

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر الطبري
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r3.claim: Qurʾān al-fajr means recitation during the dawn prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r3.anchor: أحدهما : أقم القراءة في صلاة الفجر , وهذا قول أبي جعفر الطبري .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r4.claim: It can mean the dawn prayer itself, called Qurʾān because recitation is emphasized in it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r4.anchor: الثاني : معناه صلاة الفجر , فسماها قرآنا لتأكيد القراءة في الصلاة , وهذا قول أبي اسحاق الزجاج .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r5.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r5.claim: Being witnessed means people should attend the dawn prayer at mosques.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r5.anchor: أحدهما : إن من الحكمة أن تشهده بالحضور إليه في المساجد , قاله ابن بحر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r6.claim: A prophetic report says angels of the night and day witness dawn prayer; al-Mawardi takes this to show it belongs exclusively to neither night's nor day's prayers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p263/r6.anchor: ( تشهده ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار ) وفي هذا دليل على أنها ليست من صلاة الليل ولا من صلاة النهار .

MUJAHID:v1p367#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p367#4/r1.speaker: author
MUJAHID:v1p367#4/r1.claim: The sun's decline through the nightfall refers here to sunset and the Maghrib prayer.
MUJAHID:v1p367#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ إلى غسق الليل ﴾ قال يعني غروب الشمس صلاة المغرب

MUJAHID:v1p367#4/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p367#4/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
MUJAHID:v1p367#4/r2.claim: Muḥammad b. Kaʿb al-Quraẓī identifies the Qur'an of dawn with the Fajr prayer.

MUJAHID:v1p367#4/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p367#4/r3.speaker: author
MUJAHID:v1p367#4/r3.claim: Mujahid agrees that the Qur'an of dawn refers to the Fajr prayer.
MUJAHID:v1p367#4/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد مثله

MUJAHID:v1p369#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p369#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p369#2/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the sun's duluk as its decline when it begins to decline.
MUJAHID:v1p369#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال دلوكها زيغها حين تزيغ

MUQATIL:17:78-81/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:78-81/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:78-81/r1.claim: Duluk is the sun declining from mid-sky for the first and afternoon prayers; night ghasaq is darkness after twilight for sunset and night prayers.
MUQATIL:17:78-81/r1.anchor: يعني إذا زالت الشمس عن بطن السماء، يعني عند صلاة الأولى والعصر، { إلى غسق الليل } ، يعني ظلمة الليل إذا ذهب الشفق،

MUQATIL:17:78-81/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:78-81/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:78-81/r2.claim: Qur'an of dawn means dawn-prayer recitation witnessed by angels of night and day; this verse gathers the five prayers.
MUQATIL:17:78-81/r2.anchor: يعني قرآن صلاة الغداة، { إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا } [آية: 78]، تشهده ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار، جمع صلاة الخمس

NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r1.claim: Dulūk al-shams means either its decline, making the verse cover the five prayers, or its setting, from which the author derives the noon and afternoon prayers.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس ﴾ لزوالها وعلى هذه الآية جامعة للصلوات الخمس أو لغروبها وعلى هذا يخرج الظهر والعصر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r2.claim: Ghasaq al-layl is darkness, the time for the night prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r2.anchor: ﴿ إلى غسق الليل ﴾ هو الظلمة وهو وقت صلاة العشاء

NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r3.claim: Qurʾān al-fajr means the dawn prayer, named for its recitation as a pillar; this refutes al-Aṣamm's claim that recitation is not a pillar. It may instead be named for its long recitation and is coordinated with prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r3.anchor: ﴿ وقرآن الفجر ﴾ صلاة الفجر سميت قرآنا وهو القراءة لكونها ركنا كما سميت ركوعا وسجودا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r4.claim: The dawn recitation is witnessed either by the night and day angels at their shift, making it the end of one record and start of the other, or by the many worshippers usually present.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p296#5/r4.anchor: يشهده ملائكة الليل والنهار ينزل هؤلاء ويصعد هؤلاء فهو في آخر ديوان الليل وأول ديوان النهار

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r1.claim: Dulūk is also said to mean the sun's decline from zenith, though Ibn Qutayba prefers sunset.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r1.anchor: غروبها. ويقال: زوالها. والأول أحب إلي

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r2.claim: He prefers sunset: Arab usage, including Dhū al-Rummah's الدوالك, applies dulūk to setting stars.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r2.anchor: قال ذو الرمة: مصابيح ليست باللواتي تقودها ... نجوم ولا بالآفلات الدوالك

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r3.claim: A second poem pictures the sun near sunset as a sick person pushed by the palm; one screens its rays to gauge time remaining before it sets.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر: والشمس قد كادت تكون دنفا ... أدفعها بالراح كي تزحلفا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r4.claim: Ghasaq al-layl means the darkness of night.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r5.claim: Qurʾān al-fajr means the recitation at dawn.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p259#7/r5.anchor: {غسق الليل} ظلامه. و {وقرآن الفجر} أي قراءة الفجر.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r1.claim: After describing the polytheists' schemes, God commands the Prophet to be patient and preserve prayer; prayer also seeks victory over enemies, as in 15:97.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r1.anchor: لما ذكر مكايد المشركين أمر نبيه عليه السلام بالصبر والمحافظة على

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r2.claim: Exegetes unanimously take this verse to refer to the obligatory prayers.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r2.anchor: وهذه الآية بإجماع من المفسرين إشارة إلى الصلوات المفروضة.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r3.speaker: عمر وابنه وأبو هريرة وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r3.claim: One interpretation defines the sun's duluk as its decline from the middle of the sky.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r3.anchor: أحدهما: أنه زوال الشمس عن كبد السماء قاله عمر وابنه وأبو هريرة وابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r4.speaker: علي وابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r4.claim: A second interpretation defines duluk as sunset; it is also transmitted from Ibn Abbas.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r4.anchor: الثاني أن الدلوك هو الغروب قاله علي وابن مسعود وأبي بن

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r5.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r5.claim: Al-Mawardi explains the two senses by rubbing one's eyes either from the sun's intense glare or to see it at sunset.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r5.anchor: من جعل الدلوك اسما لغروبها فلأن الإنسان يدلك عينيه براحته

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r6.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r6.claim: Abu Ubayd takes duluk as sunset and cites the expression “the sun set.”
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: دلوكها غروبها. ودلكت براح يعني الشمس أي غابت.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r7.speaker: قطرب
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r7.claim: Qutrub's verse uses birāḥ for the sun; the word is read with fatḥa as a sun-name or, in al-Farra's reading, with kasra as a plural meaning palms.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r7.anchor:
وأنشد قطرب:
هذا مقام قدمي رباح

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r8.speaker: العجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r8.claim: Al-Ajjaj's line uses rāḥ for the hand or palm that shields the eyes while pushing the sun away; Ibn al-Aʿrabi explains zahlafa as sliding on a smooth slope.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r8.anchor:
ومنه قول العجاج:
والشمس قد كادت تكون دنفا
أدفعها بالراح كي تزحلفا

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r9.speaker: ذو الرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r9.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's verse uses dālikāt for the setting stars or suns, supporting the sunset sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r9.anchor:
قال ذو الرمة:
مصابيح ليست باللواتي تقودها
نجوم ولا بالآفلات الدوالك

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya says duluk linguistically means inclination: its beginning is noon decline and its end sunset, so the interval includes Zuhr and Asr and may include Maghrib.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r10.anchor: الدلوك هو الميل في اللغة فأول الدلوك هو الزوال وآخره هو الغروب.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r11.speaker: الأوزاعي وأبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r11.claim: Some hold that Zuhr's time extends from decline to sunset because the command is tied to duluk, the whole period of inclination; Malik and al-Shafiʿi indicate this in necessity.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r11.anchor: وقد ذهب قوم إلى أن صلاة الظهر يتمادى وقتها من الزوال إلى الغروب

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by Malik, says duluk is the sun's inclination and ghassaq is night gathering into darkness.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r12.anchor: الثانية: قوله تعالى: { إلى غسق الليل } روى مالك عن ابن عباس قال: دلوك الشمس ميلها، وغسق الليل اجتماع الليل وظلمته.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r13.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r13.claim: Abu Ubayd defines ghassaq as the blackness of night, supported by Ibn Qays's poetic line.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78/r13.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الغسق سواد الليل. قال ابن قيس الرقيات:

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r1.claim: Other explanations make ghassaq the disappearance of twilight or the arrival of darkness; Zuhayr's verse uses the term at nightfall.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r1.anchor: وقد قيل: غسق الليل مغيب الشفق. وقيل: إقبال ظلمته. قال زهير:

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r2.claim: The word derives from flowing, as in an eye or wound discharging fluid; forms with and without the initial hamza are both used for nightfall.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r2.anchor: وأصل الكلمة من السيلان يقال: غسقت العين إذا سالت، تغسق.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r3.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r3.claim: On a cloudy day al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym told his muezzin to delay Maghrib until night darkened.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r3.anchor: وكان الربيع بن خثيم يقول لمؤذنه في يوم غيم: أغسق أغسق.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r4.speaker: مالك والشافعي والثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r4.claim: One view gives Maghrib a single time at sunset, based on Gabriel praying it at the same time on both days; this is the apparent Maliki position among its adherents and a well-known Shafiʿi view.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r4.anchor: فقيل: وقتها وقت واحد لا وقت لها إلا حين تحجب

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r5.speaker: مالك وأبو حنيفة وأصحابه والحسن بن حي وإسحاق وأبو ثور وداود
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r5.claim: Another view keeps Maghrib time open until twilight disappears, treating sunset-to-twilight as the full interval of ghassaq.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r5.anchor: فإذا غاب الشفق فقد خرجت من وقت المغرب ودخل وقت العشاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r6.claim: Those favoring the longer time cite Abu Musa's report that the Prophet delayed the second day's Maghrib until twilight fell, and argue this later Medinan report supersedes Gabriel's Meccan prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r6.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى بالسائل المغرب في اليوم الثاني فأخر حتى كان عند سقوط الشفق

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r7.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r7.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the longer-time ruling is the famous Maliki position, stated in the Muwattaʾ that Malik taught throughout his life.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r7.anchor: وزعم ابن العربي أن هذا القول هو المشهور من مذهب

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r8.claim: Qurtubi favors the expanded permissible time. The reports can be reconciled: Gabriel shows the preferred prompt time at sunset, while other reports show permissibility until twilight; reconciliation preserves both proofs better than abrogation or preference.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r8.anchor: قلت: القول بالتوسعة أرجح. وقد خرج الإمام الحافظ أبو محمد عبد الغني بن سعيد

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r9.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r9.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet left Mecca near sunset and did not pray Maghrib until reaching Sarf, nine miles away.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r9.anchor: عن جابر قال: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من مكة قريبا من غروب الشمس فلم يصل المغرب

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r10.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r10.claim: Al-Farra parses Qurʾān as coordinated with prayer: establish the dawn Qurʾān, meaning the dawn prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r10.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون معطوفا على الصلاة المعنى: وأقم قرآن الفجر أي صلاة الصبح قاله الفراء.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r11.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r11.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Qurʾān is accusative as an exhortation: attend to the dawn recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#2/r11.anchor: انتصب على الإغراء أي فعليك بقرآن الفجر قاله الزجاج.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r1.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r1.claim: The dawn prayer is singled out as Qurʾān because it is the greatest prayer, with long, audible recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r1.anchor: لأن القرآن هو أعظمها، إذ قراءتها طويلة مجهور بها

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r2.claim: Medinan practice favored a substantial dawn recitation that did not burden the congregation, then long recitation at Zuhr and Friday, light recitation at Maghrib, and moderate recitation at Asr and Isha; some also lighten Asr.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r2.anchor: وقد استقر عمل المدينة على استحباب إطالة القراءة في الصبح

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r3.claim: Reports of unusually short or long recitations in prayers with an established practice are set aside in favor of communal practice; the Prophet rebuked Muʿadh for beginning Isha with al-Baqara and ordered imams to keep prayer easy for people with varied needs.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r3.anchor: فافتتح سورة البقرة. خرجه الصحيح. وبأمره الأئمة بالتخفيف

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r4.claim: Calling the dawn prayer Qurʾān supports the principle that prayer requires recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r4.anchor: دليل على أن لا صلاة إلا بقراءة لأنه سمى الصلاة قرآنا.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r5.speaker: جمهور العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r5.claim: The majority require al-Fatiha from imam and solo worshipper in every rakʿa; Malik's well-known position agrees.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r5.anchor: فذهب جمهورهم إلى وجوب قراءة أم القرآن للإمام والفذ في كل ركعة.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r6.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r6.claim: Malik is also reported to require al-Fatiha in most of the prayer, a view held by Ishaq; in another report it is required in one rakʿa, according to al-Mughira and Sahnun.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r6.anchor: وعنه أيضا أنها واجبة في جل الصلاة. وهو قول إسحاق.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r7.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r7.claim: Other reports from Malik say recitation is not obligatory in any part, or only in half the prayer, the latter also attributed to al-Awzaʿi.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r7.anchor: وعنه أن القراءة لا تجب في شيء من الصلاة. وهو أشد الروايات عنه.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r8.speaker: الأوزاعي وأيوب والشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r8.claim: Al-Awzaʿi and Ayyub, and one Shafiʿi view, require recitation from imam, solo worshipper, and follower in every prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r8.anchor: وعن الأوزاعي أيضا وأيوب أنها تجب على الإمام والفذ والمأموم

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r9.claim: The Prophet says the night and day angels witness dawn prayer; Tirmidhi grades this report hasan sahih, and another route includes Abu Saʿid.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#3/r9.anchor: السادسة: قوله تعالى: { كان مشهودا } روى الترمذي عن أبي هريرة

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r1.claim: A Bukhari report says congregational prayer has twenty-five times the merit of individual prayer and night and day angels meet at dawn; Abu Hurayra cites this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r1.anchor: فضل صلاة الجميع على صلاة الواحد خمس وعشرون درجة وتجتمع ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r2.claim: The dawn prayer is performed early so both angel groups witness it; delay means only one group witnesses it. Malik and al-Shafiʿi therefore prefer praying in the pre-dawn darkness.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r2.anchor: ولهذا المعنى يبكر بهذه الصلاة، فمن لم يبكر لم تشهد صلاته إلا إحدى الفئتين

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r3.claim: Abu Hanifa prefers combining pre-dawn darkness with later brightness, and, if that is missed, prefers brightness; Qurtubi objects that this opposes the Prophet's consistent early prayer and loses the night angels' witness.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r3.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: الأفضل الجمع بين التغليس والإسفار، فإن فاته ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r4.claim: The angels' witnessing does not make dawn prayer neither night nor day: Asr also has both angel groups meeting, yet Asr is daytime by fasting and oath rulings, so dawn too belongs to daytime.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r4.anchor: وهذا مخالف لما كان عليه السلام يفعله من المداومة على

QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r5.claim: The Prophet reports that night and day angels alternate in attendance and meet at both Asr and Fajr.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:78#4/r5.anchor: يتعاقبون فيكم ملائكة بالليل وملائكة بالنهار فيجتمعون في صلاة العصر وصلاة الفجر

MAJAZ:v1p387/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p387/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p387/r1.claim: دلوك الشمس runs from its decline at noon until sunset; the explanation invokes shielding the eyes with a palm to see how much of the sun remains, and the poems by Rabāḥ and al-ʿAjjāj support its approaching sunset.
MAJAZ:v1p387/r1.anchor: «لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل» (78) ودلوك الشمس من عند زوالها إلى أن تغيب

MAJAZ:v1p387/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p387/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p387/r2.claim: غسق الليل is its darkness; Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt’s line says the night has غسقا.
MAJAZ:v1p387/r2.anchor: «إلى غسق الليل» ، أي ظلامه قال: ابن قيس الرقيات

MAJAZ:v1p387/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p387/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p387/r3.claim: قرآن الفجر means what is recited in the dawn prayer.
MAJAZ:v1p387/r3.anchor: «وقرآن الفجر» (78) أي ما يقرأ به فى صلاة الفجر

MAJAZ:v1p387/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p387/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p387/r4.claim: The dawn recitation is witnessed by the angels of night, followed after the dawn prayer by the angels of day.
MAJAZ:v1p387/r4.anchor: «إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا» (78) مجازه: إن ملائكة الليل تشهده وإذا صليت الغداة أعقبتها ملائكة النهار

RAZI-FULL:v21p21/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p21/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p21/r1.claim: The passage moves from God's doctrines about divinity, resurrection, and prophethood to the command of worship; after faith, prayer is the most excellent act of obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v21p21/r1.anchor: أردفها بذكر الأمر بالطاعات بعد الإيمان وأشرف الطاعات بعد الإيمان الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v21p21/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p21/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p21/r2.claim: After the threat that opponents might expel him, prayer directs the Prophet to persist in worship, trusting God to defeat their plots and raise his religion above theirs.
RAZI-FULL:v21p21/r2.anchor: أمره تعالى بالإقبال على عبادته لكي ينصره عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v21p21/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p21/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p21/r3.claim: On the report that Jews urged a move to Syria, the response is that God is Lord in every land and victory comes through His aid; the Prophet should continue prayer, return to his home, and ask for truthful entry and exit and a supporting authority there.
RAZI-FULL:v21p21/r3.anchor: المعبود واحد في كل البلاد وما النصرة والدولة إلا بتأييده ونصرته

RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r1.speaker: علي
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r1.claim: A view transmitted from Ali defines the sun's duluk as sunset.
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r1.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام أنه قال : دلوك الشمس غروبها

RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masud likewise says, in a report through Zirr ibn Hubaysh, that duluk is sunset.
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r2.anchor: أن عبد الله بن مسعود قال : دلوك الشمس غروبها

RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr transmits from Ibn Abbas the view that duluk is sunset.
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r3.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير هذا القول عن ابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r4.claim: Al-Farra and Ibn Qutayba adopt the sunset interpretation of duluk.
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r4.anchor: وهذا القول اختيار الفراء وابن قتيبة من المتأخرين

RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r5.claim: The majority of Companions and Successors hold that duluk is the sun's decline from its zenith.
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r5.anchor: أن دلوك الشمس هو زوالها عن كبد السماء وهو اختيار الأكثرين

RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r6.speaker: جابر
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r6.claim: A report from Jabir says that after the Prophet and Companions ate at his home, they left at noon and the Prophet identified that as the time the sun had declined.
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r6.anchor: عن جابر أنه قال : ( طعم عندي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r7.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r7.claim: Al-Kashshaf cites a report that Gabriel came at the sun's noon decline and prayed the noon prayer with the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r7.anchor: روى صاحب ( الكشاف ) عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r8.speaker: الأزهري
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r8.claim: Al-Azhari says Arabic usage calls the sun dālikah both at noon and at setting because it is declining in either case.
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r8.anchor: قال أهل اللغة معنى الدلوك في كلام العرب الزوال

RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r9.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r9.claim: Al-Qaffal says the root idea of duluk is inclination, which can describe the sun's movement toward either noon decline or sunset.

RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r10.claim: Razi prefers noon decline: since duluk means inclination and the command attaches at its onset, prayer begins when the sun first inclines from the zenith; he calls this a strong argument.
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r10.anchor: وجب أن يقال إنه أول ما حصل الميل والزوال تعلق به هذا الحكم

RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r11.speaker: الأزهري
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r11.claim: Al-Azhari also prefers noon decline because prayer from then until night includes four prayers, with dawn recitation adding the fifth; sunset would include only three, and the more useful reading is preferable.
RAZI-FULL:v21p21#2/r11.anchor: فإذا حملنا الدلوك على الزوال دخلت الصلوات الخمس في هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba cites Dhu al-Rumma’s image of setting stars to support reading dulūk as sunset; an earlier verse associates sunset with the sun’s setting.
RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r1.anchor: واحتج ابن قتيبة بقول ذي الرمة :

RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r2.claim: The sunset evidence does not exclude noon: dulūk means inclination or change, which occurs at sunset, while sunset is only one kind of such movement, as human and horse are both animals.
RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r2.anchor: الدلوك عبارة عن الميل والتغير وهذا المعنى حاصل في الغروب

RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r3.claim: Some derive dulūk from rubbing the eyes while looking at the sun and thus restrict it to sunset; al-Rāzī replies that glare makes eye-rubbing more necessary at midday, favoring the sun’s decline.
RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r3.anchor: ومنهم من احتج أيضا على صحة هذا القول بأن الدلوك اشتقاقه من الدلك

RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r4.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r4.claim: Al-Wāḥidī takes the lām in li-dulūk as causal: prayer becomes due at the sun’s decline, so it is performed on account of that decline.
RAZI-FULL:v21p22/r4.anchor: قال الواحدي : اللام في قوله لدلوك الشمس

RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r1.speaker: الكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī glosses ghassaq al-layl as the night’s darkness and says ghassaaq is the noun with fatḥa on the sīn.

RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r2.speaker: النضر بن شميل
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r2.claim: Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl defines ghassaq as the onset of night, when darkness mixes and obscures the view; al-Rāzī traces the root to flowing, as with tears or blood.
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r2.anchor: وقال النضر بن شميل : غسق الليل دخول أوله

RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r3.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r3.claim: In Ibn Jurayj’s report, ʿAṭāʾ says ghassaq is the beginning of night as it enters.
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن جريج : قلت لعطاء : ما غسق الليل

RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines ghassaq as night entering with its darkness, in response to Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq.
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r4.anchor: وسأل نافع بن الأزرق ابن عباس ما الغسق : قال دخول الليل بظلمته

RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r5.speaker: الأزهري
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r5.claim: Al-Azharī places ghassaq at the disappearance of twilight, when darkness gathers and intensifies; he compares it to an eye full of tears or a wound full of blood.
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r5.anchor: وقال الأزهري : غسق الليل عند غيبوبة الشفق عند تراكم الظلمة

RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers accumulated darkness at twilight’s disappearance: this interpretation includes all four prayers in the interval, whereas onset darkness would include only ẓuhr and maghrib.
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r6.anchor: دخلت الصلوات الأربع فيه وهي الظهر والعصر والمغرب والعشاء

RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r7.claim: If ghassaq is the first darkness, the verse names noon, first maghrib, and dawn, making noon shared by ẓuhr and ʿaṣr and first night shared by maghrib and ʿishāʾ; combining is then allowed for travel, rain, and similar excuses, not without excuse at home.
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r7.anchor: هذا يقتضي جواز الجمع بين الظهر والعصر وبين المغرب والعشاء مطلقا

RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r8.claim: If ghassaq is accumulated darkness at the disappearance of white twilight, the endpoint leaves prayer lawful before then; this fits the view that the prayers become due at red twilight.
RAZI-FULL:v21p22#2/r8.anchor: الظلمة المتراكمة إنما تحصل عند غيبوبة الشفق الأبيض وكلمة إلى لانتهاء الغاية

RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r1.claim: The commentators agree that Qurʾān al-fajr means the dawn prayer; it is coordinated with al-ṣalāh, with the sense, establish prayer and establish the dawn recitation.
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r1.anchor: أجمعوا على أن المراد منه صلاة الصبح وانتصابه بالعطف على الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r2.claim: The wording shows that prayer is not complete without recitation.
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r2.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على أن الصلاة لا تتم إلا بالقراءة

RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r3.claim: Because the command attaches recitation to dawn’s first appearance, obligation would seem to begin then; consensus removes obligation, leaving preference, so al-Rāzī says the verse supports al-Shāfiʿī’s view that praying at first light (taghlīs) is better than waiting for brightening.
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r3.anchor: هذا يدل على صحة مذهب الشافعي في أن التغليس أفضل من التنوير

RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r4.claim: Jurists hold that dawn prayer should have a longer recitation than other prayers; singling out Qurʾān at dawn marks the feature as especially complete and desirable.
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r4.anchor: السنة أن تكون القراءة في هذه الصلاة أطول من القراءة في سائر الصلوات

RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r5.speaker: الجمهور
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r5.claim: The majority say dawn prayer is witnessed because night and day angels gather behind the imam; day angels arrive during prayer, and after it night angels ascend reporting the worshippers and God’s forgiveness.
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r5.anchor: قال الجمهور : معناه أن ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار يجتمعون في صلاة الصبح

RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r6.claim: This angelic gathering supports taghlīs: night angels remain in the darkness at the prayer’s start, day angels arrive as its extended recitation brings daylight, so both witness it.
RAZI-FULL:v21p23/r6.anchor: هذا أيضا دليل قوي في أن التغليس أفضل من التنوير لأن الإنسان إذا شرع فيها

RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r1.claim: Another reading of witnessed dawn prayer is that the change from darkness to light displays God’s power; contemplating the world’s transition from death and stillness to life and motion during prayer illuminates knowledge and certainty.
RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r1.anchor: كلية هذا العالم من الظلمة إلى الضوء ومن الموت إلى الحياة ومن السكون إلى الحركة

RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r2.claim: This spiritual interpretation depends on beginning at taghlīs, when the transformation can be observed during the prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r2.anchor: هذا الاعتبار لا يحصل إلا عند أداء صلاة الفجر على سبيل التغليس

RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r3.claim: A third interpretation is witnessing through a large congregation: dawn prayer purifies hearts especially strongly, and worshippers reflect one another’s knowledge of God like facing mirrors reflecting sunlight, bringing spaciousness and comfort.
RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r3.anchor: كونه مشهودا بالجماعة الكثيرة ومزيد التحقيق فيه أنا بينا أن تأثير هذه الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r4.claim: Sleep clears the mind’s tablet of worldly impressions; rising straight into worship and recitation inscribes sacred thoughts that prevent corrupt worldly desires from taking hold, so the benefit requires prayer at first light.
RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r4.anchor: صارت ألواح عقله وفكره وخياله مطهرة عن النقوش الفاسدة الباطلة

RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r5.claim: Because love of the world, greed, envy, and rivalry are diseases of hearts, prophets act like skilled physicians; beginning obedience on waking helps reduce this hard-to-cure illness and is therefore prescribed.
RAZI-FULL:v21p24/r5.anchor: مرض حب الدنيا مستول على الخلق ولا علاج له إلا بالدعوة إلى معرفة الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v21p26/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p26/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p26/r1.claim: Although the five-prayer command is addressed to the Messenger, it applies to the community: the following night-prayer command is expressly restricted to him, so the unrestricted command cannot be Prophet-only.
RAZI-FULL:v21p26/r1.anchor: فبين أن الأمر بالتهجد مخصوص بالرسول وهذا يدل على أن الأمر بالصلاة الخمس

NAHHAS:v2p435/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p435/r10.speaker: الأخفش سعيد
NAHHAS:v2p435/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash Saʿīd parses قرآن الفجر as an object meaning prioritize dawn recitation, or as something incumbent upon the listener.
NAHHAS:v2p435/r10.anchor: بمعنى وآثر قرآن الفجر ، وعليك قرآن الفجر

NAHHAS:v2p435/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p435/r11.speaker: أبو اسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p435/r11.claim: Abū Isḥāq supplies أقم as the governing verb: establish the dawn recitation.
NAHHAS:v2p435/r11.anchor: قال أبو اسحاق : التقدير وأقم قرآن الفجر

STUDYQURAN:17:78/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r1.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r1.claim: The verse is commonly read as covering the five canonical prayers; most take the sun's decline as the beginning of decline and the time of ẓuhr, while some take it as maghrib.
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r1.anchor: This verse is commonly interpreted as alluding to all five canonical prayers

STUDYQURAN:17:78/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r2.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r2.claim: The period from sun's decline to nightfall can cover ẓuhr, ʿaṣr, maghrib, and ʿishāʾ; Shiites often combine the two afternoon and two evening prayers.
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r2.anchor: the command to perform the prayer from the declining of the sun till the darkening of the night can be understood as a reference to completing all four prayers

STUDYQURAN:17:78/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r3.speaker: some Sunni schools of law
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r3.claim: Some Sunni schools take the darkening of night simply as the sun's disappearance, while Jaʿfarī law waits until its rays disappear or the evening's middle begins.
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r3.anchor: In some Sunni schools of law, the darkening of the night may refer simply to the disappearance of the sun

STUDYQURAN:17:78/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r4.claim: Specific prayer-time interpretations may project the five prayers' regularity from middle Madinah back onto this Makkan revelation.
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r4.anchor: the various interpretations of this verse as relating to specific prayer times may, however, be a result of commentators reading the ritual regularity

STUDYQURAN:17:78/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r5.claim: The dawn recitation is the fajr prayer between dawn and sunrise, or, in one view, specifically its Quran recitation.
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r5.anchor: The recitation at dawn refers to the fifth canonical prayer, namely, the fajr prayer

STUDYQURAN:17:78/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r6.speaker: several aḥādīth
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r6.claim: The dawn recitation is witnessed by angels of both day and night.
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r6.anchor: The recitation at dawn is ever witnessed by the angels of both the day and the night

STUDYQURAN:17:78/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r7.speaker: some Sufi commentaries
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r7.claim: The prayer times also point to continuous inward prayer, the heart's remembrance and invocation of God, which is the Sufi goal.
STUDYQURAN:17:78/r7.anchor: some Sufi commentaries suggest that the command to perform the prayer at these various times throughout the day is also a reference to the importance of continuous, inward prayer

TAB-FULL:v15p22#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p22#2/r1.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v15p22#2/r1.claim: One reported interpretation takes the sun's duluk as sunset and the prayer commanded then as Maghrib.
TAB-FULL:v15p22#2/r1.anchor: وقت غروبها، والصلاة التي أمر بإقامتها حينئذ: صلاة المغرب

TAB-FULL:v15p25/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd reports his father’s view that duluk runs from the sun’s approach to setting until night darkens, describing Maghrib.
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله {أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل} [الإسراء: 78] قال: كان أبي يقول

TAB-FULL:v15p25/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r2.claim: Ibn Masud prayed Maghrib when the sun’s rim had set and swore that this was the time indicated by the verse.
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r2.anchor: كان عبد الله بن مسعود يصلي المغرب حين يغرب حاجب الشمس، ويحلف أنه الوقت

TAB-FULL:v15p25/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r3.claim: Ibrahim transmits Ibn Masud’s statement that the sun’s setting is the prayer’s time and that duluk means sunset.
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r3.anchor: عن مغيرة، عن إبراهيم، قال: قال عبد الله حين غربت الشمس

TAB-FULL:v15p25/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r4.claim: A report from Abdullah defines duluk as the sun’s inclination, meaning its movement from the zenith.
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r4.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن يزيد، عن عبد الله، قال: دلوكها: ميلها، يعني الشمس

TAB-FULL:v15p25/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas defines duluk as the sun’s zenithal decline.
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r5.anchor: عن الشعبي، عن ابن عباس، قال في قوله {أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس} [الإسراء: 78] قال: دلوكها: زوالها

TAB-FULL:v15p25/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r6.claim: Ibn Umar also says that duluk means the sun’s inclination.
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r6.anchor: عن نافع، عن ابن عمر، في قوله {أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس} [الإسراء: 78] قال: دلوكها: ميلها

TAB-FULL:v15p25/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r7.speaker: أبو برزة الأسلمي
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r7.claim: Abu Barza interprets duluk as the sun’s decline and reports that the Prophet prayed Dhuhr at that time, citing the verse.
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r7.anchor: عن أبي برزة الأسلمي، قوله {أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس} [الإسراء: 78] قال: إذا زالت

TAB-FULL:v15p25/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r8.speaker: أبو برزة
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r8.claim: Abu Barza reports that the Prophet prayed Dhuhr when the sun declined, then recited this verse.
TAB-FULL:v15p25/r8.anchor: قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي الظهر إذا زالت الشمس، ثم تلا

TAB-FULL:v15p27/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r1.claim: Hasan says Dhuhr is meant: the sun has declined from the middle of the sky and its shadow appears on the ground.
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: قال الله عز وجل لنبيه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم {أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل}

TAB-FULL:v15p27/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r2.claim: Hasan also glosses duluk simply as the sun’s zenithal decline.
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله {أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس} [الإسراء: 78] قال: دلوكها: زوالها

TAB-FULL:v15p27/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak gives the same gloss, duluk as the sun’s decline from its zenith.
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r3.anchor: عن جويبر، عن الضحاك، مثل ذلك

TAB-FULL:v15p27/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r4.claim: Abu Jaʿfar interprets the command as applying at the sun’s decline.
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r4.anchor: عن جعفر، عن أبي جعفر، في {أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس} [الإسراء: 78] قال: لزوال الشمس

TAB-FULL:v15p27/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas describes duluk as the sun’s westward shift after midday, marked by the shadow.
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r5.anchor: عن الزهري، عن ابن عباس، قال: دلوك الشمس: زيغها بعد نصف النهار

TAB-FULL:v15p27/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r6.claim: Qatadah says the sun’s duluk is when it moves from the middle of the sky, for Dhuhr.
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله {أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس} [الإسراء: 78] أي إذا زالت الشمس عن بطن السماء

TAB-FULL:v15p27/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r7.claim: Mujahid says duluk occurs when the sun inclines from its zenith.
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، {لدلوك الشمس} [الإسراء: 78] قال: حين تزيغ

TAB-FULL:v15p27/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r8.claim: Tabari prefers Dhuhr at the sun’s decline because Arabic duluk means inclination; he adduces common usage and a report using the same root for leaning.
TAB-FULL:v15p27/r8.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: عنى بقوله {أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس}

TAB-FULL:v15p28/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r1.speaker: الراجز
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r1.claim: A rajaz line about the sun and Rabah is cited as lexical evidence for “dalkat birāḥ.”
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r1.anchor: هذا مقام قدمي رباح غدوة حتى دلكت براح

TAB-FULL:v15p28/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأصمعي وأبو عمرو الشيباني
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r2.claim: With kasra, “birāḥ” describes shielding the eyes with a palm from the sun’s glare to see its setting.
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r2.anchor: فمن روى ذلك: براح، بكسر الباء، فإنه يعني: أنه يضع الناظر كفه على حاجبه

TAB-FULL:v15p28/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r3.claim: Tabari is unsure whether the gloss “birāḥ, a place” in the Ibn Masud report belongs to Abdullah or a transmitter; if Abdullah said it, his view outweighs the philologists.
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r3.anchor: ولست أدري هذا التفسير، أعني قوله: براح مكانا من كلام من هو ممن في الإسناد

TAB-FULL:v15p28/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r4.speaker: العجاج
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r4.claim: Al-Ajjaj’s verse about pushing the sun with the palm supports the philologists’ reading of “birāḥ” as the hand shielding the eyes.
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r4.anchor: فإن أهل العربية كانوا أعلم بذلك منه، ولما قال أهل الغريب في ذلك شاهد من قول العجاج

TAB-FULL:v15p28/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r5.claim: With fatḥa, “barāḥ” is a name for the sun, declined like Qatām, Hadhām, and Raqāsh.
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r5.anchor: ومن روى ذلك بفتح الباء، فإنه جعله اسما للشمس

TAB-FULL:v15p28/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r6.claim: Since duluk means inclination, once the sun leaves the zenith it has inclined west; Tabari therefore places the command at Dhuhr.
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r6.anchor: فإذا كان معنى الدلوك في كلام العرب هو الميل، فلا شك أن الشمس إذا زالت عن كبد السماء

TAB-FULL:v15p28/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r7.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r7.claim: A Prophetic report says Gabriel came at the sun’s decline and led the Prophet in Dhuhr, though Tabari notes some weakness in its chain.
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r7.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أتاني جبرائيل عليه السلام لدلوك الشمس حين زالت فصلى بي الظهر»

TAB-FULL:v15p28/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r8.speaker: أبو برزة
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r8.claim: Abu Barza reports that the Prophet prayed Dhuhr when the sun declined and then recited this verse.
TAB-FULL:v15p28/r8.anchor: قال أبو برزة: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي الظهر إذا زالت الشمس

TAB-FULL:v15p30/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r1.claim: Jabir recounts that after a meal with the Prophet and companions, the Prophet said the sun had declined as they left.
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله، قال: دعوت نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن شاء من أصحابه

TAB-FULL:v15p30/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r2.claim: A second transmission from Jabir gives the same report of the Prophet announcing the sun’s decline.
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r2.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، نحو حديث ابن حميد

TAB-FULL:v15p30/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r3.claim: If these reports are sound, the span from solar decline to nightfall includes the required Dhuhr and Asr prayers.
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r3.anchor: فبين إذن أن معنى قوله جل ثناؤه: {أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل} [الإسراء: 78]

TAB-FULL:v15p30/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r4.claim: Ghassaq is night’s arrival and approach with darkness; a line of poetry uses it of night becoming dark.
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r4.anchor: وغسق الليل: هو إقباله ودنوه بظلامه، كما قال الشاعر

TAB-FULL:v15p30/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses ghassaq as the beginning of night.
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله {أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل} [الإسراء: 78] قال: غسق الليل: بدو الليل

TAB-FULL:v15p30/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r6.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r6.claim: Ikrima likewise says ghassaq is night’s beginning.
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r6.anchor: عن أبي رجاء، قال: سمعت عكرمة، سئل عن هذه الآية: {أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل} [الإسراء: 78] قال: بدو الليل

TAB-FULL:v15p30/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p30/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: غسق الليل: غروب الشمس

TAB-FULL:v15p32/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r1.claim: Qatadah identifies ghassaq with Maghrib, the beginning of night.

TAB-FULL:v15p32/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r2.claim: Qatadah transmits a Prophetic saying that the community remains on the fitrah while it prays Maghrib before the stars appear.
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {إلى غسق الليل} [الإسراء: 78] بدو الليل لصلاة المغرب وقد ذكر لنا أن نبي الله

TAB-FULL:v15p32/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak explains ghassaq as the darkness of night.
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r3.anchor: قال: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله {إلى غسق الليل} [الإسراء: 78] يعني ظلام الليل

TAB-FULL:v15p32/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd transmits his father’s gloss of ghassaq as night’s darkness.
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد: كان أبي يقول: {غسق الليل} [الإسراء: 78] ظلمة الليل

TAB-FULL:v15p32/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r5.claim: Another view identifies the prayer at ghassaq as Asr.
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r5.anchor: عن أبي جعفر، {إلى غسق الليل} [الإسراء: 78] قال: صلاة العصر

TAB-FULL:v15p32/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r6.claim: Tabari prefers Maghrib: ghassaq is darkness after sunset, whereas Asr falls within the span from the sun’s decline to ghassaq.
TAB-FULL:v15p32/r6.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب، قول من قال: الصلاة التي أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بإقامتها عند غسق الليل

TAB-FULL:v15p33/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p33/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p33/r1.claim: The dawn prayer is witnessed by angels of the night and day.
TAB-FULL:v15p33/r1.anchor: يقول: إن ما تقرأ به في صلاة الفجر من القرآن كان مشهودا، يشهده فيما ذكر ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

TAB-FULL:v15p33/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p33/r2.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v15p33/r2.claim: The Prophet explains that angels of night and day witness the dawn recitation.
TAB-FULL:v15p33/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه الآية {وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا} [الإسراء: 78] قال: «تشهده ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار»

TAB-FULL:v15p33/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p33/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء
TAB-FULL:v15p33/r3.claim: A report from Abu al-Darda describes three divine acts in the last night hours; at dawn God and both angel watches witness the recitation.
TAB-FULL:v15p33/r3.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن الله يفتح الذكر في ثلاث ساعات يبقين من الليل

TAB-FULL:v15p33/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p33/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v15p33/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda says Ibn Masud taught that the two angel watches meet at Fajr and recited this verse.
TAB-FULL:v15p33/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، عن عقبة بن عبد الغافر، قال: قال أبو عبيدة بن عبد الله

TAB-FULL:v15p35/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p35/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p35/r1.claim: Qatadah identifies the “Quran of dawn” as the morning prayer, when night and day angel watches meet.
TAB-FULL:v15p35/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا} [الإسراء: 78] وقرآن الفجر: صلاة الصبح

TAB-FULL:v15p35/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p35/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p35/r2.claim: A second transmission from Qatadah gives the concise gloss that the Quran of dawn means the Fajr prayer.

TAB-FULL:v15p36/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r1.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r1.claim: Abdullah says the angels of day descend as the angels of night ascend at Fajr.
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله، أنه قال في هذه الآية: {وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا} [الإسراء: 78] قال: تنزل ملائكة النهار وتصعد ملائكة الليل

TAB-FULL:v15p36/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda says the night and day angel guards witness the dawn prayer.
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r2.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة، في قوله: {وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا} [الإسراء: 78] قال: يشهده حرس الليل

TAB-FULL:v15p36/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r3.claim: Ibrahim reports that the angel watches gather at Fajr, then one ascends while the other remains.
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r3.anchor: عن إبراهيم، في قوله : {وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا} [الإسراء: 78] قال: كانوا يقولون تجتمع ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

TAB-FULL:v15p36/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the Quran of dawn as the morning prayer.
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا} [الإسراء: 78] يعني صلاة الصبح

TAB-FULL:v15p36/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r5.claim: Mujahid identifies it as the morning prayer and says both angel watches gather there.
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، {وقرآن الفجر} [الإسراء: 78] قال: صلاة الصبح

TAB-FULL:v15p36/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the Quran of dawn as the morning prayer.
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r6.anchor: قال: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله {وقرآن الفجر} [الإسراء: 78] يعني صلاة الغداة

TAB-FULL:v15p36/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies it as Fajr and says angels witness it.
TAB-FULL:v15p36/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد: {وقرآن الفجر} [الإسراء: 78] قال: صلاة الفجر {إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا}

TAB-FULL:v15p37/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p37/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وأبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v15p37/r1.claim: Ali and Ubayy identify the middle prayer with Fajr: it lies between daytime and nighttime prayers and is especially liable to be missed during sleep.
TAB-FULL:v15p37/r1.anchor: وكان علي بن أبي طالب، وأبي بن كعب يقولان: الصلاة الوسطى التي حض الله عليها: صلاة الصبح

TAB-FULL:v15p37/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p37/r2.speaker: كعب
TAB-FULL:v15p37/r2.claim: Kaʿb swears that the verse refers to Fajr and that this prayer is witnessed.
TAB-FULL:v15p37/r2.anchor: عن أبي محمد الحضرمي، قال: ثنا كعب، في هذا المسجد، قال: والذي نفس كعب بيده

TAB-FULL:v15p37/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p37/r3.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v15p37/r3.claim: The Prophet says the angels of night and day gather at Fajr; Abu Hurayra cites this verse in support.
TAB-FULL:v15p37/r3.anchor: أن أبا هريرة، قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «تجتمع ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار في صلاة الفجر»

TAB-FULL:v15p37/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p37/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p37/r4.claim: Mujahid says both angel watches gather for the Fajr prayer.
TAB-FULL:v15p37/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله {وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا} [الإسراء: 78] قال: صلاة الفجر تجتمع فيها ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

TABATABAI:17:73-75/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:73-75/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:73-75/r2.claim: The passage also directs the Prophet to prayer and seeking God's protection in his comings and goings, and announces that truth will prevail.
TABATABAI:17:73-75/r2.anchor: وفي الآيات إيصاء النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بالصلوات والالتجاء بربه

TABATABAI:17:75-77/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:75-77/r6.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:17:75-77/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī says dulūk is the sun's decline; al-Mubarrad takes it as the span from decline to sunset, while another view identifies it with sunset.
TABATABAI:17:75-77/r6.anchor: قال في مجمع البيان الدلوك الزوال

TABATABAI:17:75-77/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:75-77/r7.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:17:75-77/r7.claim: The lexicon explains “decline” through the observer rubbing the eyes at the sun's brightness, whether at its zenith or setting.
TABATABAI:17:75-77/r7.anchor: وأصله من الدلك فسمي الزوال دلوكا لأن الناظر إليها يدلك عينيه

TABATABAI:17:75-77/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:75-77/r8.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:17:75-77/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī glosses ghasaq al-layl as the onset of darkness, while al-Raghib's lexicon gives its intense darkness.
TABATABAI:17:75-77/r8.anchor: وقال فيه غسق الليل ظهور ظلامه

TABATABAI:17:75-77/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:75-77/r9.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
TABATABAI:17:75-77/r9.claim: Reports transmitted through the Shi'i routes interpret dulūk as noon's decline and nightfall as midnight, covering the four prayers from noon through night.
TABATABAI:17:75-77/r9.anchor: والمروي عن أئمه أهل البيت عليهم السلام من طرق الشيعة تفسير دلوك الشمس بزوالها وغسق الليل بمنتصفه

TABATABAI:17:78-80/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:78-80/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:78-80/r1.claim: The interval from noon to midnight contains four daily prayers; adding the dawn prayer named Qur'an al-fajr completes the five obligatory prayers.

TABATABAI:17:78-80/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:78-80/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:78-80/r2.claim: Qur'an al-fajr is grammatically coordinated with prayer and means the dawn prayer because it includes recitation; reports agree on this interpretation.
TABATABAI:17:78-80/r2.anchor: والمراد به صلاة الصبح لما تشمل عليه من القراءة وقد اتفقت الروايات

TABATABAI:17:78-80/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:78-80/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:78-80/r3.claim: Reports from both traditions agree that night and day angels witness the dawn prayer.
TABATABAI:17:78-80/r3.anchor: بأنه يشهده ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

TABATABAI:17:73-81/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:73-81/r6.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
TABATABAI:17:73-81/r6.claim: A report says the five prayers took their present form in Medina after Islam grew strong: seven units were added to the noon, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers, while dawn remained as prescribed in Mecca so night and day angels could witness it.
TABATABAI:17:73-81/r6.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن سعيد بن المسيب عن علي بن الحسين عليه السلام قال قلت له متى فرضت الصلاة

TABATABAI:17:73-81/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:73-81/r7.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:17:73-81/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī says the verse explains the obligation and times of the five prayers; he cites a supporting report through al-Ayyashi and Ubayd ibn Zurara.
TABATABAI:17:73-81/r7.anchor: قال ففي الآية بيان وجوب الصلوات الخمس وبيان أوقاتها ويؤيد ذلك ما رواه العياشي بالإسناد عن عبيد بن زرارة

TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r1.claim: The continuation of Ubayd ibn Zurara's report from Abu Abd Allah divides the four prayers into two from noon to sunset and two from sunset to midnight, each pair in order.
TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r1.anchor: قال إن الله افترض أربع صلوات أول وقتها من زوال الشمس إلى انتصاف الليل

TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r2.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that Gabriel came at the sun's decline and prayed the noon prayer with the Prophet.
TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء
TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Darda reports the Prophet's recitation and explanation that God and the night and day angels witness the dawn prayer.
TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال قرء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r4.claim: The interpretation of dawn recitation as witnessed by night and day angels is nearly mass-transmitted in both traditions; some reports add God's and the Muslims' witness.
TABATABAI:17:73-81#2/r4.anchor: تفسير كون قرآن الفجر مشهودا في روايات الفريقين بشهادة ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار يكاد يبلغ حد التواتر

TABRISI:17:78-81/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81/r1.speaker: المبرد
TABRISI:17:78-81/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad defines dulūk as the interval from the sun’s decline until sunset; another view makes it sunset itself.
TABRISI:17:78-81/r1.anchor: قال المبرد دلوك الشمس من لدن زوالها إلى غروبها وقيل هو الغروب

TABRISI:17:78-81/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:78-81/r2.claim: Dulūk derives from rubbing: observers rub their eyes against the sun’s glare, either at its decline or when discerning it at sunset.
TABRISI:17:78-81/r2.anchor: فسمي الزوال دلوكا لأن الناظر إليها يدلك عينيه لشدة شعاعها

TABRISI:17:78-81/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81/r3.speaker: ثعلب
TABRISI:17:78-81/r3.claim: Thaʿlab says the sun has tilted when described as dālikat.

TABRISI:17:78-81/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81/r4.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:17:78-81/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains barāḥ as the sun’s decline, when the observer shades the eyes with a palm; he cites a rajaz line about the sun declining while Rabāḥ stands there.
TABRISI:17:78-81/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج: يقال دلكت براح وبراح أي مالت للزوال

TABRISI:17:78-81/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:78-81/r5.claim: With fatḥa, barāḥ is a proper name for the sun on the pattern of Qaṭām and Ḥadhām; with kasra, it means the observer’s palm, as al-Farrāʾ explains.
TABRISI:17:78-81/r5.anchor: ومن قال براح بفتح الباء جعلها اسما للشمس مبنيا على فعال

TABRISI:17:78-81/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:78-81/r6.claim: Ghasaq denotes the onset or appearance of night’s darkness; the same root describes a bursting sore revealing what is inside.
TABRISI:17:78-81/r6.anchor: وغسق الليل ظهور ظلامه يقال غسقت القرحة إذا انفجرت فظهر ما فيها

TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r2.claim: Qurʾān al-fajr is accusative by an understood command, aqim; nāfilatan laka is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier.
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r2.anchor: قرآن الفجر منصوب على تقدير وأقم قرآن الفجر وانتصب قوله نافلة لك

TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r3.claim: After setting out proofs and warning, God commands the Prophet—and by extension others—to establish prayer from the sun’s decline to nightfall.
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r3.anchor: ثم أمر سبحانه بعد إقامة البينات وذكر الوعد والوعيد بإقامة الصلاة

TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, Jābir, and several Successors take dulūk as the sun’s decline, making the commanded prayer ẓuhr; this is also transmitted from al-Bāqir and al-Ṣādiq.
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r4.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس بخلاف وابن عمر وجابر وأبي العالية والحسن

TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r5.speaker: النخعي
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r5.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and al-Suddī take dulūk as sunset, making the prayer maghrib; this is also reported from Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās.
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r5.anchor: وهو قول النخعي والضحاك والسدي والصلاة المأمور بها على هذا

TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r6.claim: The author prefers decline because it lets the passage encompass all five obligatory prayers rather than only one prayer time.
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r6.anchor: والقول الأول هو الأوجه لتكون الآية جامعة للصلوات الخمس

TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r7.claim: On the preferred reading, decline-time prayers are ẓuhr and ʿaṣr, nightfall prayers are maghrib and later ʿishāʾ, and Qurʾān al-fajr is dawn prayer.
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r7.anchor: صلاتا دلوك الشمس الظهر والعصر وصلاتا غسق الليل هما المغرب والعشاء الآخر

TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda call ghasaq the first onset of night; Mujāhid calls it sunset, al-Jubbāʾī its darkness, and al-Bāqir and al-Ṣādiq midnight.
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r8.anchor: وهو أول بدء الليل عن ابن عباس وقتادة وقيل هو غروب الشمس عن مجاهد

TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r9.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r9.claim: Some companions infer that ẓuhr’s time extends to the end of the day because the verse makes the interval from decline to nightfall a prayer time.
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r9.anchor: واستدل قوم من أصحابنا بالآية على أن وقت صلاة الظهر موسع إلى آخر النهار

TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r10.speaker: الشيخ أبو جعفر
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r10.claim: Shaykh Abū Jaʿfar rejects that inference: sunset concerns maghrib until twilight, while decline may summarize all five prayers rather than one prayer’s time.
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r10.anchor: ولم يرتضه الشيخ أبو جعفر قدس الله روحه قال: لأن من قال إن الدلوك

TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r11.claim: The author answers that decline to nightfall can be shared time for four prayers: ẓuhr and ʿaṣr share decline-to-sunset, and maghrib and ʿishāʾ share sunset-to-nightfall.
TABRISI:17:78-81#2/r11.anchor: جعل من دلوك الشمس الذي هو الزوال إلى غسق الليل وقتا للصلوات الأربع

TABRISI:17:78-79/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-79/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:78-79/r1.claim: The verse establishes the obligation and timing of five prayers, singling out dawn prayer as Qurʾān al-fajr.
TABRISI:17:78-79/r1.anchor: ففي الآية بيان وجوب الصلوات الخمس وبيان أوقاتها

TABRISI:17:78-79/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-79/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:17:78-79/r2.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī transmits from ʿUbayd b. Zurāra that Abū ʿAbd Allāh assigns two prayers from decline to sunset and two from sunset to midnight, ordered within each pair.
TABRISI:17:78-79/r2.anchor: عن عبيد بن زرارة عن أبي عبد الله ع وفي هذه الآية قال

TABRISI:17:78-79/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-79/r3.speaker: المرتضى
TABRISI:17:78-79/r3.claim: Al-Murtaḍā adopts this account of the prayer times.
TABRISI:17:78-79/r3.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب المرتضى علم الهدى قدس روحه في أوقات الصلوات

TABRISI:17:78-79/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-79/r4.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:17:78-79/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the separate mention of Qurʾān al-fajr shows prayer must include recitation.
TABRISI:17:78-79/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: إن في قوله وقرآن الفجر فائدة عظيمة

TABRISI:17:78-79/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-79/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:78-79/r5.claim: All commentators say dawn prayer is witnessed by angels of night and day; the Prophet’s congregational-prayer report is cited from al-Bukhārī’s Ṣaḥīḥ.
TABRISI:17:78-79/r5.anchor: كلهم قالوا معناه أن صلاة الفجر تشهدها ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار

TABRISI:17:78-79/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:78-79/r6.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:17:78-79/r6.claim: The Prophet says congregational prayer is twenty-five times superior to individual prayer and night and day angels assemble for dawn prayer; al-Bukhārī includes it in his Ṣaḥīḥ.
TABRISI:17:78-79/r6.anchor: تفضل صلاة الجماعة صلاة أحدكم وحده بخمسة وعشرين جزءا

THALABI:v6p120/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p120/r1.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
THALABI:v6p120/r1.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi and several other authorities interpret the sun's dulūk as sunset, supported by poetic usage.
THALABI:v6p120/r1.anchor: قال إبراهيم النخعي ومقاتل بن حيان والسدي ويمان وابن زيد: دلوكها غروبها

THALABI:v6p120/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p120/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p120/r2.claim: The name “براح” refers to the sun; its kasra variant describes shading one's eyes to see its remaining light as it sets.
THALABI:v6p120/r2.anchor:
وبراح اسم للشمس مثل قطام وجذام ورفاش.
ويروى، براح بكسر الباء

THALABI:v6p120/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p120/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v6p120/r3.claim: Ibn Masud prayed Maghrib and broke his fast at sunset, swearing this was the appointed time meant by the verse.
THALABI:v6p120/r3.anchor: ودليل هذا التأويل حديث عبد الله بن مسعود إنه كان إذا غرب الشمس صلى المغرب

THALABI:v6p120/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p120/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p120/r4.claim: Another large group, including Ibn Abbas and al-Shafiʿi, interprets dulūk as the sun's decline from its zenith.
THALABI:v6p120/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عمرة وابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله وأبو العالية وعطاء وقتادة

THALABI:v6p120/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p120/r5.speaker: أبو مسعود عقبة بن عمرو
THALABI:v6p120/r5.claim: The Prophet said Gabriel came at the sun's decline and led him in the noon prayer.
THALABI:v6p120/r5.anchor: حديث أبي مسعود عقبة بن عمرو قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أتاني جبرئيل

THALABI:v6p120/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p120/r6.speaker: أبو برزة
THALABI:v6p120/r6.claim: Abu Barza says the Prophet prayed noon at the sun's decline and then recited this verse.
THALABI:v6p120/r6.anchor: وقال أبو برزة: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي الظهر إذا زالت الشمس

THALABI:v6p120/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p120/r7.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
THALABI:v6p120/r7.claim: After eating at Jabir's home, the Prophet left at noon and told Abu Bakr that this was when the sun had declined.
THALABI:v6p120/r7.anchor: قال جابر بن عبد الله: دعوت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن شاء من أصحابه فطعموا عندي

THALABI:v6p121/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p121/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p121/r1.claim: On the noon-decline interpretation, the verse gathers all prayer times: dulūk covers noon and afternoon prayers, and nightfall covers the evening prayers; Gabriel's first instruction was noon.
THALABI:v6p121/r1.anchor: وعلى هذا التأويل يكون الآية جامعة لمواقيت الصلاة كلها، فدلوك الشمس صلاة الظهر والعصر

THALABI:v6p121/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p121/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v6p121/r2.claim: A report from the Prophet describes Gabriel teaching the five prayer times on two successive days, with different shadow and twilight limits, and says to keep to the prophetic times.
THALABI:v6p121/r2.anchor: وروى محمد بن عمار عن أبي هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «جاءني جبرئيل

THALABI:v6p121/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p121/r3.speaker: جابر
THALABI:v6p121/r3.claim: Jabir reports Gabriel leading the Prophet and congregation through prayer times over two days, demonstrating each prayer in turn.
THALABI:v6p121/r3.anchor: عطاء بن أبي رياح عن جابر قال: أن جبرئيل أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يعلمه مواقيت الصلاة

THALABI:v6p121#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p121#2/r1.speaker: جابر
THALABI:v6p121#2/r1.claim: The continuation says Gabriel prayed dawn with the stars still visible on the second day, then declared the interval between the two demonstrations to be the prayer time.
THALABI:v6p121#2/r1.anchor: ثم ابتدأ الفجر وأصبح والنجوم بادية مشتبكة فصنع كما صنع بالأمس

THALABI:v6p121#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p121#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p121#2/r2.claim: Gabriel demonstrated the prayer times twice at the Kaaba: the first day's early limits and the second day's later limits bound the permitted time for each prayer.
THALABI:v6p121#2/r2.anchor: وعن نافع بن جبير بن مطعم عن عبد الله بن عباس إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أتاني جبرئيل

THALABI:v6p121#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p121#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p121#2/r3.claim: Nightfall begins with the onset of darkness.
THALABI:v6p121#2/r3.anchor:
إلى غسق الليل إقباله بظلامه.
قال ابن عباس: بدو الليل

THALABI:v6p121#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p121#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p121#2/r4.claim: Qatada interprets ghassaq as the Maghrib prayer.

THALABI:v6p121#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p121#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v6p121#2/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda takes ghassaq to mean the darkness of night.

THALABI:v6p121#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p121#2/r7.speaker: ابن قيس الرقيات
THALABI:v6p121#2/r7.claim: The poet's use of “غسقا” describes night growing dark and supports the lexical explanation.
THALABI:v6p121#2/r7.anchor:
ابن قيس الرقيات:
إن هذا الليل قد غسقا … فاشتكيت الهم والأرقا

THALABI:v6p121#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p121#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p121#2/r8.claim: “Qur'an of dawn” means the dawn prayer, named for its required recitation, or the recitation read during that prayer.
THALABI:v6p121#2/r8.anchor: وقرآن الفجر أي صلاة الفجر فسمى الصلاة قرآنا لأنها لا تجوز إلا بقرآن

THALABI:v6p121#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p121#2/r9.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v6p121#2/r9.claim: Al-Farra parses “Qur'an of dawn” as coordinated with prayer: establish the dawn recitation.
THALABI:v6p121#2/r9.anchor: وانتصاب القرآن من وجهين: أحدهما: أنه عطف على الصلاة أي أقم قرآن الفجر

THALABI:v6p121#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p121#2/r10.speaker: أهل البصرة
THALABI:v6p121#2/r10.claim: The Basrans parse it as an exhortation: attend to the Qur'an of dawn.
THALABI:v6p121#2/r10.anchor: وقال أهل البصرة: على [الإغراء] أي وعليك بقرآن الفجر

THALABI:v6p121#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p121#2/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p121#2/r11.claim: Another grammatical view treats the dawn recitation as an appositional explanation of establishing prayer at the sun's decline.
THALABI:v6p121#2/r11.anchor: وقال بعضهم: اجتماعه وبيانه وحينئذ يكون مجاز أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس

THALABI:v6p121#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p121#2/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p121#2/r12.claim: Dawn is witnessed by the angels of night and day as one group descends while the other ascends; this supports the prayer's obligation from the start of its time and the merit of praying early.
THALABI:v6p121#2/r12.anchor: يشهد ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار ينزل هؤلاء ويصعد هؤلاء

THALABI:v6p121#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p121#2/r13.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v6p121#2/r13.claim: The Prophet reports a twenty-five-degree merit for congregational prayer and says night and day angels assemble at dawn prayer.
THALABI:v6p121#2/r13.anchor: الزهوي عن أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «فضل صلاة الجميع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r1.claim: One view takes the sun's duluk as sunset; Farra adduces a line using dalakat for setting, and Ibn Qutayba also cites Dhu al-Rumma.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r2.claim: The other view is the sun's decline from its zenith; Nafi and Salim report Ibn Umar saying duluk is its movement at noon, and Ibn Abbas reports the shadow turning or the sun's decline.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r2.anchor: فروى نافع وسالم عن ابن عمر قال: دلوك الشمس: زيغها حين تزول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r3.speaker: جابر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r3.claim: Jabir reports that after dining with the Prophet and companions, they left when the sun declined, and the Prophet identified that as the time the sun had duluk.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r3.anchor: ما روي عن جابر أنه قال: طعم عندي رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r4.claim: Reports from Ibn Masud take duluk as sunset; Ali, Ibn Abbas through Said ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd agree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r4.anchor: أن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: دلوك الشمس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r5.claim: Zajjaj says duluk is the sun's inclination at either noon or sunset; Mubarrad defines its range as noon decline through sunset.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج: دلوك الشمس زوالها وميلها في وقت الظهر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r6.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r6.claim: Al-Azhari prefers noon decline because that reading makes the command cover all five prayers; taking duluk as sunset would cover only three.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p428/r6.anchor: وقال الأزهري: القول عندي في دلوك الشمس أنه زوالها نصف النهار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r1.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r1.claim: Duluk means the sun's decline because it has moved from its place at noon or sunset; the lām in Quran al-fajr gives the reason or purpose, since prayer becomes due at noon decline.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r1.anchor: ومعنى الدلوك في كلام العرب: الزوال، ولذلك قيل للشمس إذا زالت نصف النهار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r2.speaker: الفراء والزجاج وأبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r2.claim: These authorities define ghasaq al-layl as the darkness or blackness of night.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r2.anchor: غسق الليل: سواده وظلمته، قاله الفراء والزجاج وأبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r3.speaker: ابن شميل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r3.claim: Ibn Shumayl says ghasaq is the entering beginning of night, when darkness mixes and blocks the view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r3.anchor: قال ابن شميل: غسق الليل دخول أوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r4.claim: Abu Zayd derives the word from flowing: an eye gushes with discharge and water; a poem uses ghasiq for something flowing, and ghasaq al-layl is darkness pouring down.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r4.anchor: قال أبو زيد: غسقت العين تغسق، وهو هملان العين بالغمص والماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r5.speaker: ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r5.claim: Al-A'rabi glosses ghasaq as pouring out and says the sky ghasaq when it drizzled; Umar's phrase means night descended over the hills.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r5.anchor: وروى ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي: الغسقان: الانصباب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas defines ghasaq as night gathering and becoming dark; Ibn Masud says it is nightfall darkness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: غسق الليل: اجتماع الليل وظلمته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r7.speaker: ابن جريج عن عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj asks Ata, who says ghasaq is the beginning of night as it comes in.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r7.anchor: قال ابن جريج: قلت لعطاء: ما غسق الليل؟

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
