WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r8.claim: In answer to Nafi ibn al-Azraq, Ibn Abbas says ghasaq is night entering with darkness and cites Zuhayr's verse about the onset of darkness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r8.anchor: وسأل نافع بن الأزرق ابن عباس: ما الغسق؟ قال: دخول الليل بظلمته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r9.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r9.claim: Al-Azhari identifies ghasaq with disappearance of the red twilight, the time of the final evening prayer; with noon duluk this covers the five prayers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p433/r9.anchor: وقال الأزهري: غسق الليل عندي: غيبوبة الشفق الأحمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p435/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p435/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p435/r1.claim: Quran al-fajr means the dawn prayer; Ibn Masud, Mujahid, Masruq, Qatada, and the exegetes generally agree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p435/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد صلاة الصبح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p436/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p436/r4.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p436/r4.claim: Farra and Zajjaj take Quran al-fajr as coordinated with the command to establish prayer; Zajjaj infers that prayer must include recitation because prayer is named Quran.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p436/r4.anchor: وانتصابه على أنه معطوف بالعطف على الصلاة في قوله: {أقم الصلاة}

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:77-79/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:77-79/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:77-79/r2.claim: Prayer from the sun's decline at noon to nightfall includes noon, afternoon, and the two evening prayers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:77-79/r2.anchor: من وقت زوالها { إلى غسق الليل } إقباله بظلامه، فيدخل في هذا صلاة الظهر والعصر والعشاءين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:77-79/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:77-79/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:77-79/r3.claim: Quran at dawn means the dawn prayer, called Quran because prayer is invalid without recitation; angels of night and day witness it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:77-79/r3.anchor: { وقرآن الفجر } يعني: صلاة الفجر، سماها قرآنا لأن الصلاة لا تصح إلا بقراءة القرآن. { إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا } تشهده ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r4.claim: Qatada defines the sun’s dulūk as its decline from the middle of the sky, marking noon prayer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r4.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: إذا زالت الشمس عن بطن السماء لصلاة الظهر.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r5.claim: Qatada defines ghasaq al-layl as the beginning of night, marking sunset prayer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r5.anchor: إلى غسق الليل} [الإسراء: 78] قال: بدو الليل لصلاة المغرب.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r6.claim: Yahya takes dulūk as the sun’s decline from the zenith, covering noon prayer and then afternoon prayer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r6.anchor: قال يحيى: يقول لزوال الشمس عن كبد السماء، يعني صلاة الظهر والعصر بعدها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r7.claim: Ghasaq is night’s onset, gathering, and darkness: sunset is at its beginning, while night prayer is when it darkens and twilight disappears.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r7.anchor: بدو الليل واجتماعه وظلمته. صلاة المغرب عند بدو الليل، وصلاة العشاء عند اجتماع الليل،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas defines dulūk as the sun’s shadow turning back and ghasaq as night gathering into darkness.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r8.anchor: مالك بن أنس، عن داود بن الحصين، أن ابن عباس قال: دلوك الشمس: إذا فاء الفيء، وغسق الليل:

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r9.claim: Ibn Umar defines dulūk as the sun’s inclination.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r9.anchor: مالك بن أنس، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر، قال: دلوك الشمس ميلها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r10.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r10.claim: Hasan reports that Gabriel led the Prophet in teaching the five prayers; at noon the Prophet led people in four quiet rakʿahs of noon prayer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r10.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، عن الحسن، أن رسول الله لما جاء بالصلوات الخمس إلى قومه خلى عنهم، حتى إذا زالت الشمس

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r11.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r11.claim: In Hasan’s report, the Prophet led four quiet afternoon rakʿahs after the sun declined and remained bright, following Gabriel’s lead.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r11.anchor: فاجتمعوا، فصلى بهم العصر أربع ركعات دون صلاة الظهر، لا يعلن فيهن القراءة، جبريل بين يدي نبي الله،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r12.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r12.claim: The same report says the Prophet began sunset prayer at sunset with three rakʿahs; its recitation account continues in the next segment.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p153/r12.anchor: فصلى بهم المغرب ثلاث ركعات يعلن في

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r1.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r1.claim: Hasan’s report says the Prophet led three sunset rakʿahs, reciting aloud in the first two but not the last, with Gabriel leading him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r1.anchor: الركعتين الأوليين ولا يعلن في الركعة الآخرة، جبريل بين يدي نبي الله،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r2.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r2.claim: The Prophet led four night prayers, reciting aloud in the first two rakʿahs and quietly in the last two, under Gabriel’s lead.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r2.anchor: فصلى بهم العشاء أربع ركعات يعلن في الركعتين الأوليين ولا يعلن في الآخرتين

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r3.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r3.claim: After these prayers, people spent the night unsure whether any more prayers would be prescribed.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r3.anchor: ثم بات الناس ولا يدرون أيزادون على ذلك أم لا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r4.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r4.claim: At dawn the Prophet led two long morning rakʿahs and recited aloud, following Gabriel.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r4.anchor: فصلى بهم الصبح ركعتين أطالهما وأعلن فيهما القراءة، جبريل بين يدي نبي الله،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r5.claim: Alqama and al-Aswad transmit Ibn Masud’s view that dulūk is sunset.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r5.anchor: المعلى، عن الأعمش، عن إبراهيم، عن علقمة والأسود، عن ابن مسعود، قال: دلوكها غروبها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r6.claim: Ibn Masud said after sunset that this was the appointed time for the prayer, then recited the verse.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r6.anchor: غابت الشمس فقال عبد الله بن مسعود: والذي لا إله غيره إن هذه الساعة لميقات هذه الصلاة،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r7.speaker: المسعودي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r7.claim: Al-Masudi says Ibn Masud took dulūk as sunset and ghasaq as night’s arrival, with the prayer interval between them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r7.anchor: قال المسعودي: فدلوكها حين تغيب في قول عبد الله، وغسق الليل: مجيء الليل والصلاة فيما بينهما.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r8.claim: Yahya says Ibn Abbas’s interpretation of dulūk as the sun’s decline is the general view, referring to noon prayer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r8.anchor: قال يحيى: وتفسير ابن عباس: هو زوالها، هو قول العامة، يعني وقت صلاة الظهر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r9.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r9.claim: Al-Suddi argues that if dulūk meant decline, prayer would only cover the span between decline and sunset.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r9.anchor: قال السدي، وكان يعالج التفسير: لو كان دلوك الشمس زوالها لكانت الصلاة فيما بين زوالها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r10.speaker: المسعودي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r10.claim: Al-Masudi preferred Ibn Abbas’s interpretation of dulūk as the sun’s decline.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154/r10.anchor: وكان قول ابن عباس أعجب إلى المسعودي

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r1.claim: Qatada identifies Qurʾān al-fajr as the dawn prayer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r1.anchor: قوله: {وقرءان الفجر} [الإسراء: 78] قال قتادة: وهي صلاة الصبح.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r2.claim: Angels of night and day witness the dawn prayer, meeting then and at the afternoon prayer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r2.anchor: يشهده ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار، يجتمعون عند صلاة الصبح وعند صلاة العصر فيما

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r3.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that God asks the angels how they left His servants; they answer that they found and left them praying.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي: " فيسألهم ربهم وهو أعلم بهم فيقول:

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masud said the two angelic guards meet at sunset, as transmitted by Abu Ubayda.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r4.anchor: عن عقبة بن عبد الغافر، أن أبا عبيدة بن عبد الله بن مسعود كتب إليه أن عبد الله بن مسعود كان يقول عند صلاة المغرب:

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة بن عبد الله بن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda says it was commonly related that the guards of night and day meet at dawn.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r5.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، عن عقبة بن عبد الغافر، عن أبي عبيدة بن عبد الله بن مسعود، قال: كنا نحدث أن عند صلاة الفجر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r6.claim: Ibn Masud says the angelic guards meet at dawn and sunset, citing the verse about the witnessed dawn recitation.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p154#2/r6.anchor: المسعودي، عن عمرو بن مرة، عن أبي عبيدة، عن ابن مسعود، قال: يتدارك الحرسان عند صلاة الصبح والمغرب.

ELMALILI:17:78-79/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:78-79/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:78-79/r1.claim: The command is to maintain prayer; the sun’s decline until nightfall spans the noon, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers.
ELMALILI:17:78-79/r1.anchor: Güneş’in dülûkü, yani zevâli dolayısıyla gece karanlığına kadar ki öğle, ikindi, akşam, yatsı vakitlerini

ELMALILI:17:78-79/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:78-79/r2.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:17:78-79/r2.claim: A report says Gabriel came at the sun’s decline and led the Prophet in the noon prayer.
ELMALILI:17:78-79/r2.anchor: Şems’in dülûkünde zeval bulduğu vakit Cibrîl geldi, bana öğle namazını kıldırdı

ELMALILI:17:78-79/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:78-79/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:78-79/r3.claim: Qur’an at dawn means the dawn prayer, whose recitation is especially important.
ELMALILI:17:78-79/r3.anchor: sabah Kur’ân’ını da yani kıraati bilhassa mühim olan sabah namazını da ikāme et

ELMALILI:17:78-79/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:78-79/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:78-79/r4.claim: Both the night and day angels attend and witness the dawn prayer; all nature wakes and human awareness of witnessing rises.
ELMALILI:17:78-79/r4.anchor: Ona gece melâikesi de gündüz melâikesi de hâzır ve şâhid olur ve bütün fıtrat uyanır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r1.claim: The discussion shifts from divinity, afterlife, and prophethood to prayer, the most important worship; commentators say this verse, revealed after the Isra prayer obligation, indicates the five daily prayers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r1.anchor: beş vakit namaza işaret edildiği belirtilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r2.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r2.claim: Duluk can mean the sun passing its zenith toward sunset, or completing three quarters of its apparent daily circle (the afternoon), and is also used for sunset; Ibn Ashur therefore includes noon, afternoon, and evening.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r2.anchor: İbn Âşûr’a göre “dülûkü’ş-şems” deyimi, öğle, ikindi ve akşam vakitlerini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r3.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur takes the particle ila as indicating that duluk includes more than one prayer time.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r3.anchor: “ilâ” edatının da bu deyimin birden fazla vakti içerdiğine işaret etmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r4.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r4.claim: Shawkani lists three readings of duluk: the sun’s decline from zenith, sunset, or the period from decline until sunset; Razi calls the first the majority view.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r4.anchor: Şevkânî bu deyimin anlamıyla ilgili görüşleri şöyle sıralar: a) Zeval vakti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r5.claim: Ghasaq means darkness and refers to night prayer after all twilight disappears; Quran al-fajr refers to morning prayer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r5.anchor: şafağın tamamının kaybolduğu yatsı vaktini ifade eder; “kur’ânü’l-fecr” ise sabah

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r6.claim: Quran al-fajr also implies recitation within prayer generally, though dawn prayer is singled out as an example and the Prophet recited more at dawn.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r6.anchor: bu bütün namazlar için gerekli olmakla birlikte burada sabah namazının örnek olarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r7.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r7.claim: On one reading, duluk covers noon and afternoon, ghasaq covers evening and night, and Quran al-fajr covers dawn, yielding three named periods for five prayers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r7.anchor: dülûkü’ş-şems” öğle ve ikindiyi, “gasaku’l-leyl” akşam ve yatsıyı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r8.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r8.claim: Razi infers that pairing noon with afternoon and evening with night permits combining those prayers; other evidence limits combining to reasons such as travel.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:78/r8.anchor: mutlak olarak bu namazların cem edilebileceğini

SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r1.claim: The lām in لدلوك may mean after, supported by Mutammim ibn Nuwayra's poem and the idiom كتبته لثلاث خلون.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r1.anchor: أحدهما: أنها بمعنى " بعد " ، أي: بعد دلوك الشمس، ومثله قول متمم بن نويرة:

SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r2.speaker: متمم بن نويرة
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r2.claim: His poem فلما تفرقنا كأني ومالكا لطول اجتماع لم نبت ليلة معا uses lām with the sense after.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r2.anchor:
3090- فلما تفرقنا كأني ومالكا
لطول اجتماع لم نبت ليلة معا

SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r3.speaker: الواحدي
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r3.claim: Alternatively, the lām has its ordinary purposive sense, because prayer becomes obligatory at the sun's decline, according to al-Wahidi.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنها على بابها، أي: لأجل دلوك. قال الواحدي: " لأنها إنما تجب بزوال الشمس "

SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r4.claim: Duluk is a verbal noun of دلكت الشمس; its best-known meaning is noon, while another view spans noon to sunset.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r4.anchor: والدلوك: مصدر دلكت الشمس، وفيه ثلاثة أقوال، أشهرها: أنه الزوال، وهو نصف النهار.

SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari derives the term from rubbing, since a person rubs the eye when looking at the sun; the author says this phrasing makes دلوك seem not to be a verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " واشتقاقه من الدلك؛ لأن الإنسان يدلك عينه عند النظر إليها "

SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r6.claim: The author's objection is that this implies دلوك is not a verbal noun because al-Zamakhshari derives it from the verbal noun الدلك.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r6.anchor: وهذا يفهم أنه ليس بمصدر؛ لأنه جعله مشتقا من المصدر.

SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r7.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r7.claim: A third view takes دلوك as sunset; al-Farraʾ cites a poem in which دلكت براح means the sun set.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r7.anchor:
والثالث: أنه الغروب، وأنشد الفراء عليه قوله:
3091- هذا مقام قدمي رباح

SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r8.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r8.claim: In al-Farraʾ's poem, براح is the sun and دلكت means setting.

SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r9.speaker: ابن قتيبة
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r9.claim: Ibn Qutayba cites Dhu al-Rumma's line about non-setting stars to support interpreting الدوالك as those that set.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r9.anchor:
وأنشد ابن قتيبة على ذلك قول ذي الرمة:
3092- مصابيح ليست باللواتي تقودها
نجوم ولا بالآفلات الدوالك

SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r10.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r10.claim: Al-Raghib says duluk is the sun's decline toward sunset and links it to pushing it with the palm; he lists related meanings for rubbing, delaying, perfume rubbed by hand, and a butter-and-date dish.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78/r10.anchor: وقال الراغب: دلوك الشمس ميلها للغروب، وهو من قولهم: دلكت الشمس: دفعتها بالراح،

SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r1.claim: ‘Until nightfall’ attaches to ‘establish’ and marks the prayer’s endpoint; ‘at the sun’s decline’ attaches to the same verb.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r1.anchor: في هذا الجار وجهان، أحدهما: أنه متعلق ب أقم " فهي لانتهاء غاية الإقامة، وكذلك اللام في " لدلوك " متعلقة به أيضا.

SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the phrase attaches to an omitted predicate as a circumstantial of ‘prayer’: establish it extending until nightfall.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه متعلق بمحذوف على أنه حال من " الصلاة " ، أي: أقمها ممدودة إلى غسق الليل، قاله أبو البقاء.

SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r3.claim: The alternative is problematic as grammatical analysis because it posits a restricted existential as governor; it works as an explanation of meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r3.anchor: وفيه نظر: من حيث إنه قدر المتعلق كونا مقيدا، إلا أن يريد تفسير المعنى لا الإعراب.

SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r4.speaker: ابن شميل
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r4.claim: Al-ghasaq means the beginning of night; an anonymous line uses the verb for night setting in.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r4.anchor: والغسق: دخول أول الليل، قاله ابن شميل. وأنشد:

SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r5.claim: Another view defines al-ghasaq as night’s blackness, deriving the image from liquid flowing over the world.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو سواد الليل وظلمته، وأصله من السيلان: غسقت العين، أي: سال دمعها

SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r6.claim: An eye may be full of tears and a wound full of blood; thus darkness is pictured as filling existence.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r6.anchor: ويقال: غسقت العين: امتلأت دمعا، وغسق الجرح: امتلأ دما، فكأن الظلمة ملأت الوجود.

SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r7.claim: The quoted anonymous verse uses الغسق for darkness descending.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r7.anchor: 3094- ظلت تجود يداها وهي لاهية حتى إذا هجم الإظلام والغسق

SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r8.claim: For ‘a ghasq’ in 113:3, one view means the moon when eclipsed and darkened, another means night.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r8.anchor:
والغاسق في قوله:
ومن شر غاسق
[الفلق: 3] قيل: المراد به القمر إذا كسف واسود. وقيل: الليل.

SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r9.claim: Al-ghassaq, with either light or doubled consonant, is fluid draining as pus from Hell’s people.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r9.anchor: والغساق بالتخفيف والتشديد ما يسيل من صديد أهل النار.

SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r10.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r10.claim: Arabic pairs غسق/أغسق, ظلم/أظلم, دجى/أدجى, and غبش/أغبش.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#2/r10.anchor: ويقال: غسق الليل وأغسق، وظلم وأظلم، ودجى وأدجى، وغبش وأغبش، نقله الفراء.

SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r1.claim: ‘Qur’an of dawn’ may be coordinated with ‘prayer’: establish the dawn prayer, named by one of its constituent acts.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r1.anchor: والمراد به صلاة الصبح، عبر عنها ببعض أركانها.

SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r2.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r2.claim: A second parse makes the phrase an exhortative accusative, with an implied ‘you must attend to’ understood.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r2.anchor: أنه منصوب على الإغراء، أي: وعليك قرآن الفجر، كذا قدره الأخفش وتبعه أبو البقاء،

SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r3.claim: Basran principles reject this parse because verbal nouns used as verbs cannot govern when omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r3.anchor: وأصول البصريين تأبى هذا؛ لأن أسماء الأفعال لا تعمل مضمرة.

SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r4.claim: A third parse supplies an omitted verb meaning ‘increase’ or ‘adhere to’ the dawn recitation.
SAMIN-DURR:17:78#3/r4.anchor: الثالث: أنه منصوب بإضمار فعل، أي: كثر قرآن أو الزم قرآن الفجر.

ZAJJAJ:v3p254/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p254/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p254/r4.claim: Dulūk al-shams can mean its decline at noon or its tilt toward sunset; at noon it is said the sun has inclined until its glare must be screened with the palm.
ZAJJAJ:v3p254/r4.anchor:
دلوك الشمس زوالها وميلها في وقت الظهيرة، وكذلك ميلها إلى
الغروب هو دلوكها أيضا،

ZAJJAJ:v3p254/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p254/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p254/r5.claim: Arab usage says the sun has dalakat biraḥ when it inclines from its zenith and one shades the eyes with a palm.
ZAJJAJ:v3p254/r5.anchor:
يقال: قد دلكت براح وبراح.
أي قد مالت للزوال حتى صار الناظر يحتاج إذا تبصرها أن يكسر
الشعاع عن بصره براحته.

ZAJJAJ:v3p254/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p254/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p254/r6.claim: An unnamed poet uses dalakat biraḥ as evidence for the expression describing the sun’s tilt.
ZAJJAJ:v3p254/r6.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
هذا مقام قدمي رباح. . . للشمس حتى دلكت براح

ZAJJAJ:v3p255/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p255/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p255/r1.claim: Ghasaq al-layl means the darkness of night.
ZAJJAJ:v3p255/r1.anchor:
وقوله: (إلى غسق الليل).
أي ظلمة الليل.

ZAJJAJ:v3p255/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p255/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p255/r2.claim: Qurʾān al-fajr means ‘establish the dawn recitation’; the wording shows prayer must include recitation because dawn prayer itself is called Qurʾān.
ZAJJAJ:v3p255/r2.anchor: حتى سميت الصلاة قرآنا، فلا تكون صلاة إلا بقراءة.

ZAJJAJ:v3p255/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p255/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p255/r3.claim: Exegetical reports say both night angels and day angels attend the dawn recitation.
ZAJJAJ:v3p255/r3.anchor:
جاء في التفسير أن ملائكة الليل يحضرون قراءة الفجر، وملائكة النهار
يحضرونها أيضا.

ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n95/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n95/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n95/r1.claim: The verse, read with the Prophet's practice, establishes the five obligatory daily prayers for adult men and women and their times.
ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n95/r1.anchor: this verse fully circumscribes the five daily prayers laid down in Islam as obligatory for every adult man and woman

ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n95/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n95/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n95/r2.claim: Dawn recitation stands for the morning prayer because the Prophet lengthened its recitation, emphasizing its special significance.
ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n95/r2.anchor: the Prophet, under divine inspiration, used to lengthen his recitation while praying at that time

ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n96/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n96/r1.speaker: classical commentators
ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n96/r1.claim: Most classical commentators understand dawn prayer as witnessed by the angels of both night and day.
ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n96/r1.anchor: Most of the classical commentators take this to mean

ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n96/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n96/r2.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n96/r2.claim: Razi identifies the witness as God's illuminating spark in the soul, heightening perception at dawn and enabling spiritual insight through prayer.
ASAD-NOTES:17:78#n96/r2.anchor: Razi, however, is of the opinion that the "witness" to which the Qur'an refers here is the spark of God-given illumination in man's own soul

QIRAAT-ER:17:78:10#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:17:78:10#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:17:78:10#1/r1.claim: Dropping the hamza in Qurān is a dialectal phonetic simplification without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:17:78:10#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant dropping the hamza -- qurān instead of qurʾān; reflects dialectal hamza-dropping

QIRAAT-ER:17:78:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:17:78:13#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:17:78:13#1/r1.claim: This variant reads Qurān without hamza, a dialectal simplification identical to the other word's variant.
QIRAAT-ER:17:78:13#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant without hamza -- dialectal simplification; identical to word 9 variant

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r1.claim: Qatāda defines the sun's dulk as its decline from the middle of the sky.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس ﴾ قال دلوكها حتى تزيغ عن بطن السماء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r2.claim: Qatāda identifies ghasaq al-layl with the Maghrib prayer and Qurʾān al-fajr with the Fajr prayer.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r2.anchor: و ﴿ غسق الليل ﴾ صلاة المغرب ﴿ وقرآن الفجر ﴾ صلاة الفجر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r3.claim: Qatāda says both night and day angels witness Fajr prayer.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r3.anchor: قال قتادة وأما قوله ﴿ كان مشهودا ﴾ فيقول ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار يشهدون تلك الصلاة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUmar defines dulk as the sun's decline after midday, marking the time of Ẓuhr.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r4.anchor: عن الزهري عن سالم عن ابن عمر في قوله تعالى ﴿ لدلوك الشمس ﴾ قال دلوكها ميلها بعد نصف النهار وهو وقت الظهر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r5.speaker: طاوس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r5.claim: Ṭāwūs, from his father, and ʿIkrima both define dulk as sunset.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r5.anchor: عن ابن طاوس عن أبيه وعن إسماعيل بن شروس عن عكرمة قالا دلوكها غروبها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r6.speaker: عطاء
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ defines dulk as the sun's decline and ghasaq as the start of night.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r6.anchor: قلت لعطاء ما دلوكها قال ميلها قال قلت فما غسق الليل قال أوله حين يدخل

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r7.speaker: عبد الله
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r7.claim: ʿAbd Allāh says the sun has dūlikat biraḥ when it sets, explaining biraḥ as a place.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r7.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق عن الأسود عن عبد الله أنه قال حين غربت الشمس دلكت براح يعني براح مكانا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through Mujāhid, also defines dulk as sunset.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس قال دلوكها غروبها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r9.claim: Abū Hurayra confirms that dulk is after the sun passes its zenith and says to pray Ẓuhr then, followed by ʿAṣr while the sun remains bright.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r9.anchor: إذا زالت الشمس عن بطن السماء أو عن كبد السماء بعد نصف النهار قال نعم قال فصل حينئذ الظهر ثم صل العصر والشمس بيضاء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r10.claim: Abū Hurayra says Maghrib follows sunset, ʿIshāʾ follows disappearance of twilight and darkening, and praying before the horizon's whiteness fades is preferable.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r10.anchor: قال قلت نعم غروب الشمس قال نعم قال فاحدرها في إثرها ثم احدرها في إثرها وصل صلاة العشاء إذا ذهب الشفق وادلأم الليل

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r11.claim: Abū Hurayra says Fajr begins when whiteness spreads across the horizon, cautions against certain sitting postures and forgetfulness, and identifies the middle prayer as ʿAṣr.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r11.anchor: إذا اصطفق الأفقان بالبياض قال نعم فصلها حينئذ إلى الشرق وقال في حديثه وإياك والحبوة والإقعاء وتحفظ من السهو

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r12.claim: In the same exchange, Abū Hurayra points to al-Fātiḥa as the seven oft-repeated verses and asks about the Qurʾānic ablution verse.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p384/r12.anchor: قال أتقرأ من القرآن شيئا قال قلت نعم قال اقرأ قال فقرأت فاتحة القرآن قال فقال هذه السبع المثاني التي يقول الله

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p393/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p393/r1.speaker: طاوس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p393/r1.claim: Ṭāwūs says dulk is sunset, ghasaq is Maghrib, and Qurʾān al-fajr is Fajr; night and day angels gather at Fajr and report how much each worshipper omitted or added.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p393/r1.anchor: عن ابن طاوس عن أبيه قال ﴿ لدلوك الشمس ﴾ غروبها ﴿ إلى غسق الليل ﴾ المغرب ﴿ وقرآن الفجر ﴾ صلاة الفجر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p393/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p393/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p393/r3.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says Nebuchadnezzar was successively transformed into a lion, vulture, and bull while retaining human reason; after God restored his spirit, he proclaimed that only heaven's God is true.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p393/r3.anchor: سمعت وهب بن منبه يحدث أن بختنصر مسخ أسدا فكان ملك السباع ثم مسخ نسرا فكان ملك الطير

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p393/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p393/r4.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p393/r4.claim: Wahb says the People of the Book disagreed whether Nebuchadnezzar died a believer: some said he repented, while others rejected that view because he killed prophets, burned books, and destroyed Jerusalem.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p393/r4.anchor: فقيل لوهب بن منبه أمؤمن مات قال وجدت أهل الكتاب قد اختلفوا فيه فقال بعضهم قد آمن قبل أن يموت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r1.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r1.claim: Al-Farra says دلوك means sunset; his poetic citation’s براح names the sun and دلكت means it set.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r1.anchor: الدلوك الغروب قاله الفراء وابن قتيبة، واستدل الفراء بقول الشاعر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba cites Dhu al-Rumma’s phrase الآفلات الدوالك as evidence concerning the setting sun.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r3.claim: Another view defines دلوك as the sun’s midday decline; its derivation is from rubbing because a person rubs the eye when looking at the sun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r3.anchor: وقيل: الدلوك زوال الشمس نصف النهار. قيل واشتقاقه من الدلك لأن الإنسان تدلك عينه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r4.claim: A further view uses دلوك for the period from the sun’s decline until sunset.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r4.anchor: وقيل الدلوك من وقت الزوال إلى الغروب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r5.claim: غسق means the darkness of night; al-Kisaʾi explains the verb and noun forms, while al-Nadr ibn Shumayl says it is night’s beginning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r5.anchor: الغسق سواد الليل وظلمته. قال الكسائي غسق الليل غسوقا والغسق الاسم بفتح السين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r6.speaker: النضر بن شميل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r6.claim: Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl defines the onset of غسق as the beginning of night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r6.anchor: وقال النضر بن شميل: غسق الليل دخول أوله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r7.claim: The cited line إن هذا الليل قد غسقا illustrates غسق used of night becoming dark.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r7.anchor: قال الشاعر: إن هذا الليل قد غسقا ... واشتكيت الهم والأرقا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r8.claim: The root can mean flowing: the eye flows with water and الغاسق is something flowing, likened to darkness pouring over the world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r8.anchor: وأصله من السيلان غسقت العين تغسق هملت بالماء والغاسق السائل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r9.claim: The second cited poem illustrates darkness setting and غسق.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r9.anchor: قال الشاعر: ظلت تجود يداها وهي لاهية ... حتى إذا جنح الإظلام والغسق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r10.claim: Asked by Nafi ibn al-Azraq what غسق means, Ibn Abbas answered: night in its darkness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r10.anchor: وسأل نافع بن الأزرق ابن عباس ما الغسق؟ قال: الليل بظلمته،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r11.claim: The expression غسقت العين can also describe an eye filled with blood.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r12.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r12.claim: Al-Farra lists several related expressions for night’s darkening.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p93#3/r12.anchor: وحكى الفراء غسق الليل واغتسق وظلم وأظلم ودجى وأدجى وغبش وأغبش،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r1.claim: After discussing the plot against the Messenger, God commands him to devote himself to worship rather than let them occupy his heart; prayer is the noblest act after faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r1.anchor: ومناسبة أقم الصلاة لما قبلها أنه تعالى لما ذكر كيدهم للرسول وما كانوا يرومون به،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r2.claim: The command to establish prayer addresses the Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r2.anchor: وتقدم الكلام في إقامة الصلاة والمواجه بالأمر الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r3.claim: Some take the lām in لدلوك as meaning after, as in the cited elegy and the idiom writing something after three days of a month have passed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r3.anchor: واللام في لدلوك قالوا: بمعنى بعد أي بعد دلوك الشمس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r4.speaker: الواحدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r4.claim: Al-Wahidi takes the lām as causal: prayer is due because the sun has declined.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r4.anchor: وقال الواحدي: اللام للسبب لأنها إنما تجب بزوال الشمس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya says exegetes unanimously take this verse to refer to the prescribed prayers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطية: أقم الصلاة الآية هذه بإجماع من المفسرين إشارة إلى الصلوات المفروضة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r6.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس وأبو بردة والحسن والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r6.claim: They define دلوك as the sun’s decline, assigning the times to noon and afternoon prayers, nightfall to sunset and night prayers, and قرآن الفجر to dawn prayer; this covers all five prayers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r6.anchor: فقال ابن عمر وابن عباس وأبو بردة والحسن والجمهور: دلوك الشمس زوالها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r7.claim: On that view the verse assigns المغرب and العشاء to nightfall and صلاة الصبح to Qur’an at dawn, encompassing every prescribed prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r7.anchor: والإشارة إلى الظهر والعصر وغسق الليل إشارة إلى المغرب والعشاء وقرآن الفجر أريد به صلاة الصبح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r8.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Gabriel came to the Prophet at the sun’s decline and prayed noon prayer with him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r8.anchor: وروى ابن مسعود أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أتاني جبريل عليه السلام لدلوك الشمس حين زالت فصلى بي الظهر»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r9.speaker: جابر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r9.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet came out after eating when the sun had declined and told Abu Bakr that this was the time it declined.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r9.anchor: وروى جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج من عنده وقد طعم وزالت الشمس، فقال: «اخرج يا أبا بكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r10.claim: They define دلوك as sunset, assigning it to Maghrib, غسق to nightfall and Isha, and قرآن الفجر to dawn prayer; this interpretation does not cover noon and afternoon prayers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97/r10.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود وابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم: دلوك الشمس غروبها والإشارة بذلك إلى المغرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r1.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r1.claim: Ali identifies duluk al-shams as sunset.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r2.claim: The prepositions lam and ila attach to aqim, with ila marking the endpoint of the prayer period.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r2.anchor: وتتعلق اللام وإلى بأقم، فتكون إلى غاية للإقامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows the phrase to be circumstantial from prayer, meaning prayer extended through the period.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r3.anchor: أن تكون حالا من الصلاة قال: أي ممدودة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r4.claim: Qur'an al-fajr means the dawn prayer, named for its recitation, which is lengthy and audible; the phrase is coordinated with prayer.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r5.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash parses Qur'an al-fajr as accusative after an omitted verb, either preferring it or making it incumbent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r5.anchor: وقال الأخفش: انتصب بإضمار فعل تقديره وآثر قرآن الفجر أو عليك قرآن الفجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says dawn prayer is called Qur'an because recitation is a pillar, as prayer is also named for bowing, prostration, and qunut.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r6.anchor: سميت صلاة الفجر قرآنا وهي القراءة لأنها ركن كما سميت ركوعا وسجودا وقنوتا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r7.claim: This naming supports the view that recitation is a pillar, against the claim of Ali ibn Abi Aliya and al-Asamm that it is not.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r8.claim: If duluk means noon, one reading distributes the wording over three shared time boundaries: noon, sunset, and dawn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r8.anchor: كان الوقت مشتركا بين الظهر والعصر إذا غييت الإقامة بغسق الليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r9.claim: The apparent wording commands prayer over one interval ending at nightfall, or from sunset to nightfall, plus dawn; it does not yield all five prayer times.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r9.anchor: ولا تؤخذ أوقات الصلوات الخمس من هذا اللفظ بوجه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r10.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r10.claim: Al-Razi argues that the command to recite at dawn proves recitation is obligatory in prayer, since no other recitation is obligatory then.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r10.anchor: دلالة على أن الصلاة لا تتم إلا بالقراءة لأن الأمر على الوجوب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r11.claim: Al-Razi rejects taking Qur'an al-fajr as the dawn prayer: it makes literal Qur'an metaphorical without evidence, and night vigil cannot be dawn prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r11.anchor: لأنه صرف الكلام عن حقيقته إلى المجاز بغير دليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r12.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r12.claim: Al-Razi takes the pronoun in fihi as the Qur'an itself; even if it meant prayer, naming prayer for recitation still makes recitation a pillar.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r12.anchor: فثبت أن المراد حقيقة القرآن لا مكان التهجد بالقرآن المقروء في صلاة الفجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r13.claim: The apparent command favors performing dawn prayer early; consensus prevents treating the first moment of dawn as obligatory, leaving recommendation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r13.anchor: والظاهر ندبية إيقاع صلاة الصبح في أول الوقت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r14.claim: Repeating Qur'an al-fajr instead of using a pronoun magnifies and honors the dawn recitation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r14.anchor: وأعاد قرآن الفجر في قوله إن قرآن الفجر ولم يأت مضمرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r15.claim: Witnessed means witnessed by the angels guarding night and day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p97#2/r15.anchor: ومعنى مشهودا تشهده الملائكة حفظة الليل وحفظة النهار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r1.speaker: الرسول
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r1.claim: A prophetic report says the night and day angels alternate and gather at dawn and afternoon prayers; this is the majority explanation of witnessed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r1.anchor: إنهم يتعاقبون ويجتمعون في صلاة الصبح وصلاة العصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r2.claim: The majority say the dawn recitation is witnessed by the night and day angels, as stated in the report.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r3.claim: One alternative says many worshippers ordinarily witness the dawn prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r3.anchor: وقيل يشهده الكثير من المصلين في العادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r4.claim: Another alternative says the dawn prayer deserves to be witnessed by a large congregation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r4.anchor: من حقه أن تشهده الجماعة الكثيرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads Qur'an al-fajr as an exhortation to lengthen dawn recitation so more people hear the Qur'an and reward increases; dawn is therefore the longest recitation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r5.anchor: حثا على طول القراءة في صلاة الفجر لكونها مكثورا عليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r6.speaker: محمد بن سهل بن عسكر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar says God and His angels witness the dawn recitation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r7.claim: A report from Abu al-Darda says God descends in the final part of the night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r7.anchor: وذكر حديث أبي الدرداء أنه تعالى ينزل في آخر الليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan dismisses al-Razi's discussion of witnessed as alien to ordinary Arabic and insists on the Prophet's explanation by the night and day angels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r8.anchor: والذي ينبغي بل لا يعدل عنه ما فسره به الرسول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r9.speaker: الترمذي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r9.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades the report about the night and day angels حسن صحيح.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p98/r9.anchor: وقال فيه الترمذي حديث حسن صحيح

TABRISI:13:11/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:11/r5.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:13:11/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says four angels assemble at dawn prayer; he links this to the statement that the dawn recitation is witnessed, a report also transmitted from the imams.
TABRISI:13:11/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن هم أربعة أملاك يجتمعون عند صلاة الفجر وهو معنى قوله:

BURHAN:v2p484/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p484/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p484/r5.claim: The first reason to repeat an explicit noun instead of using a pronoun is to magnify or honor it; examples include repeated mention of God, the Quran's dawn recitation, and Zechariah.
BURHAN:v2p484/r5.anchor: وللخروج على خلاف الآصل أسباب أحدها قصد التعظيم

BURHAN:v2p488/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p488/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p488/r4.claim: Repeating “Qurʾān at dawn” rather than saying “it” prevents the pronoun from seeming to refer to dawn itself.
BURHAN:v2p488/r4.anchor: وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا

BURHAN:v4p341/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p341/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p341/r2.claim: In the command to pray from the sun’s decline, lām can mean after.
BURHAN:v4p341/r2.anchor: وبمعنى بعد نحو ﴿ أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس

BURHAN:v4p341/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p341/r3.speaker: ابن أبان
BURHAN:v4p341/r3.claim: Ibn Abān says the apparent sense of lām here is causal.
BURHAN:v4p341/r3.anchor: وقال ابن أبان الظاهر أنها للتعليل

ITQAN:v3p194/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p194/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p194/r2.claim: Repeating the explicit name can signal exaltation; al-Baqara 2:282 exemplifies this through repeated mention of Allah.
ITQAN:v3p194/r2.anchor: ومنها قصد التعظيم نحو ﴿ واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله والله بكل شيء عليم ﴾

ITQAN:v4p519#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p519#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p519#2/r4.claim: A report from Umar has the Prophet explain the sun's dُلūk as its decline from the zenith; a second report from Ibn Umar gives the same explanation but has a weak chain.
ITQAN:v4p519#2/r4.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ﴿ أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس ﴾ قال ( لزوال الشمس )

ITQAN:v4p519#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p519#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p519#2/r5.claim: Al-Tirmidhi authenticates, and al-Nasa'i transmits, the Prophet's explanation that angels of night and day witness the dawn recitation.
ITQAN:v4p519#2/r5.anchor: قال ( تشهد ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار )

ITQAN:v2p497/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p497/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p497/r1.claim: The lām is a preposition, subjunctive particle, jussive particle, or non-governing particle; the preposition is usually kasra with an overt noun and fatha with a pronoun, apart from yāʾ.
ITQAN:v2p497/r1.anchor: أربعة أقسام جارة وناصبة وجازمة ومهملة غير عاملة

ITQAN:v2p497/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p497/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p497/r2.claim: The lām may mark entitlement or a relation between a meaning and its possessor, as in praise belonging to God and woe belonging to the defrauders.
ITQAN:v2p497/r2.anchor: الاستحقاق وهي الواقعة بين معنى وذات

ITQAN:v2p497/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p497/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p497/r3.claim: Lām can indicate a particular relationship or attachment, as in someone having a father or siblings.
ITQAN:v2p497/r3.anchor: والاختصاص نحو ﴿ إن له أبا ﴾ ﴿ فإن كان له إخوة ﴾

ITQAN:v2p497/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p497/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p497/r4.claim: Lām can indicate ownership, as in God's possession of what is in the heavens and earth.
ITQAN:v2p497/r4.anchor: والملك نحو ﴿ له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ﴾

ITQAN:v2p497/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p497/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p497/r10.claim: Lām can mean 'in' for the Day of Resurrection or its appointed time; 'for my life' may mean during my life or, alternatively, for the sake of the afterlife.
ITQAN:v2p497/r10.anchor: أي في حياتي وقيل هي فيها للتعليل أي لأجل حياتي في الآخرة

ITQAN:v2p497/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p497/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p497/r12.claim: In 'for the sun's dُلūk', lām may carry the sense 'after'.
ITQAN:v2p497/r12.anchor: وبعد نحو ﴿ أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس ﴾

ITQAN:v3p98/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p98/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p98/r4.claim: The reverse figure names a part for the whole: 'face' means God's essence or the person facing, body-wide states are expressed by faces or hands, and prayer's standing, reciting, bowing, or prostrating can stand for the whole prayer.
ITQAN:v3p98/r4.anchor: عبر بالوجوه عن جميع الأجساد لأن التنعم والنصب حاصل بكلها

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda relates Qur’an to a she-camel’s not having gathered a fetus in her womb; his anonymous verse uses qaraʾat to mean carrying a fetus.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r1.anchor:
وأنشد أبو عبيدة:
هجان اللون لم تقرأ جنينا (5)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r3.claim: Qur’an can be a verbal noun, like qirāʾa.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r3.anchor: ويكون القرآن مصدرا كالقراءة: يقال: قرأت قراءة حسنة وقرآنا حسنا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r4.claim: Qur’an al-fajr means the recitation at dawn, that is, the dawn prayer; a poet’s line about ʿUthmān uses Qur’an to mean recitation.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p33#2/r4.anchor:
قال الشاعر في عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه-:
ضحوا بأشمط عنوان السجود به ... يقطع الليل تسبيحا وقرآنا (1)

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r1.claim: Two glosses give ghassaq as the onset or entry of night as darkness falls.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r1.anchor: والمسألة فى (ظ، وق) عن (إلى غسق الليل) قال فى (ظ) : إذا أظلم، وفى (وقب) : دخول الليل بظلمته

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r2.speaker: ابن السكيت
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit defines the root as night entering and mixing with darkness; ghassaq is its beginning darkness.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r2.anchor: قال ابن السكيت في باب صفة الليل: وغسق الليل دخول أوله حين اختلط

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r3.claim: The four Quranic forms from this root are ghassaq in 17:78, ghāsiq in 113:3, and ghassāq in 38:57 and 78:25.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r3.anchor: وهذه الكلمات الأربع هي كل ما في القرآن من المادة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r4.claim: Zuhayr, and in one textual version al-Nabigha, are cited as poetic witnesses for ghassaq as dark night.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p575/r4.anchor: والشاهد بيت زهير، ظلت وفى (ظ) بيت النابغة: وكأنَّ ما قالوا وما وعدوا. . . إلٌّ تضمنَه من دامس غسقُ

NASHR:v1p414/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p414/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v1p414/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr transfers the hamza’s vowel in these Quran forms, including Quran al-fajr, qurʾānan farraqnāhu, and fa-ttabiʿ qurʾānahu.

NASHR:v1p414/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p414/r5.speaker: سيبويه
NASHR:v1p414/r5.claim: Sībawayh treats the definite article as lām alone, with the preceding alif a connecting hamza; despite being written attached, the lām behaves as a separate particle for transfer.
NASHR:v1p414/r5.anchor: لام التعريف هي عند سيبويه حرف واحد من حروف التهجي، وهو اللام وحدها، وبها يحصل التعريف

NASHR:v1p414/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p414/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p414/r6.claim: Other grammarians treat the article as alif plus lām, with hamza omitted in connected speech; they cite its retention or easing under transfer, its behavior after interrogative hamza, and its cut form in vocative Allāh.
NASHR:v1p414/r6.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى أن أداة التعريف هي: الألف واللام، وأن الهمزة تحذف في الدرج تخفيفا لكثرة الاستعمال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r1.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r1.claim: Al-Shihab says the Fatiha encompasses two of the three modes of signification: implication and entailment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r1.anchor: من أن ذلك لإشتمالها على دلالة التضمن والإلتزام وهما ثلثا الدلالات

ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r2.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r2.claim: Al-Dailami reports from Abu al-Darda that the Fatiha suffices where no other Quran passage does and outweighs the Quran sevenfold on the scales; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r2.anchor: ولو أن فاتحة الكتاب جعلت في كفة الميزان وجعل القرآن في الكفة الأخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r3.claim: Al-Alusi says the report most naturally promises multiplied reward, which conflicts with the preceding explanation and the view he quotes.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r3.anchor: فأنه لا يتبادر منه إلا الفضل في الثواب فيعارض ظاهره ذلك الخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r4.claim: He offers several reconciliations: the reports concern successive stages of reward, differing circumstances, equivalence to two thirds, or Quran understood as prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r4.anchor: ويمكن التوفيق بين الخبرين وبه يزول الإشكال بأن الأول كان أولا وتضاعف الثواب ثانيا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r5.claim: One reconciliation takes Quran in one or both reports to mean prayer, as in this verse; its merit varies with people’s levels of recitation and prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r5.anchor: أو بأن القرآن في أحد الخبرين أو فيهما بمعنى الصلاة مثله في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r6.claim: Reported explanations of the name Fatiha call it the best surah, equal in sanctity to the whole Quran, the refuge of believers, or the mother of the Book as a decisive surah; Al-Alusi says naming reasons need not apply uniformly.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r6.anchor: لأنها أفضل السور أو لأن حرمتها كحرمة القرآن كله أو لأن مفزع أهل الإيمان إليها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r7.claim: Although the Fatiha gathers the Book’s meanings, its seven absent letters may show that spiritual completeness does not require formal completeness; their number matches its verses, and they are dark letters absent from the ambiguous opening sequences.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r7.anchor: لعل ذلك للإشارة إلى أن الكمال المعنوي لا يلزمه الكمال الصوري ولا ينقصه نقصانه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r8.claim: Al-Alusi says every luminous letter occurs in the Fatiha while only seven dark letters occur, signifying beauty’s predominance over majesty and the repeated language of mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r8.anchor: وهي النورانية المشتملة عليها بأسرها الفاتحة للإشارة إلى غلبة الجمال على الجلال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r9.claim: Pairing luminous and dark letters symbolizes believers whose faith is unmixed and those whose faith is mixed with sin; this affirms that sin does not erase faith, and yields three classes as in 35:32.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r9.anchor: وإذا طوبقت الآحاد يحصل نوراني معه ظلماني ونوراني خالص إشارة إلى قسمي المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r10.claim: He interprets the dark-only, luminous-only, and mixed forms as the sinful, pure believer, and mixed believer, respectively, linking the scheme to the three classes in 35:32.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r10.anchor: يظهر سر التثليث في ( فمنهم ظالم لنفسه ومنهم مقتصد ومنهم سابق بالخيرات

ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r11.claim: Why precisely these seven letters were omitted is a secret known to some; their being dotted letters hints at concealment and doubt, an obscure allusion Al-Alusi presents tentatively.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r11.anchor: نعم في كون الساقط معجما فقط إشارة إلى أن الغين في العين والرين في البين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r12.claim: Al-Alusi says the hints he can discern are slight beside the secrets revealed to mystics immersed in the Quran’s depths.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r12.anchor: وهذا ما يلوح لأمثالنا من أسرار كتاب الله تعالى وأين هو مما يظهر للعارفين الغارقين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r13.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r13.claim: Al-Razi explains the missing letters as allusions to punishment: thubur, Jahannam, disgrace, infernal sounds, zaqqum, misery, the three-forked shade, laza, and separation; Al-Alusi dismisses this as lacking real investigation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p36/r13.anchor: ولمولانا العلامة فخر الدين الرازي في هذا المقام كلام ليس له في التحقيق أدنى إلمام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p56/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p56/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p56/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that people who gather in a mosque to recite and study Qur'an receive sakina and mercy, are surrounded by angels, and are mentioned by God among those near Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p56/r1.anchor: ما اجتمع قوم في بيت من بيوت الله، يتلون كتاب الله، ويتدارسونه فيما بينهم، إلا نزلت عليهم السكينة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p56/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p56/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p56/r2.claim: Some Qur'an commentators say the dawn recitation is witnessed by angels; a hadith from Abu Hurayra explains that night and day angels meet at dawn and afternoon prayers and report finding the servants praying.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p56/r2.anchor: وجاء في بعض التفاسير: أن الملائكة تشهده. وقد جاء في الصحيحين عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه
